summary_zh: 以下信件发表在2025年12月的《旗帜》杂志上。这本书是应一位读者的要求出版的，他认为这本书很有帮助，希望它的忠告也能祝福他人。您也可以在Banner播客上收听这封信的阅读。尊敬的[…]《讲道中的陷阱：一封关于申请的信》（ Pitfalls in Preaching: A Letter on Application ）一文首次出现在美国真理旗帜
title_zh: 讲道中的陷阱：一封关于申请的信
content: The following letter was published in the December 2025 issue of the Banner Magazine. It is published here at the request of a reader who found it helpful, in the hope that its counsel might be blessed to others also. You can also listen to a reading of this letter on the Banner Podcast. Dear J______, Following our conversation about application in preaching, I thought I would send along some thoughts I have had over the years on the subject. I want to point out some pitfalls you may want to keep in mind as you train R______. The only reason I know about them is from spending too much time in them myself! There has been a lot of self–examination and repenting over the years for me in this matter. The first thought is that too often (even in some of the best books on preaching) we hear that the text drives the sermon. This is a half-truth. A potentially dangerous half-truth. I have seen a man so intent on expositing his text well (and he did it very well) that he did not seem to notice or care that a third of the people in the room walked out before he finished preaching because he went on so long and the last meal of the conference was being served to meet the constraint of local train times. A wrong type of focus on the text and its explanation can make us oblivious to the very people the text is for. A preacher who stands up to preach having spent ninety per cent of his sermon preparation time in the week concentrating on the biblical text has not sufficiently realized what preaching actually is. In their book Letters Along the Way D. A. Carson and John Woodbridge put it this way: A chief reason why so much of what passes for evangelical expository preaching is so boring and irrelevant is that the preacher has spent a vastly disproportionate amount of preparation time in exegesis and outlines, and so little in thinking through how the Word of God is to wound and heal (to use the language of Hosea). 1 So preaching is about people. Preaching is about what God has to say to people about their lives . The text for a sermon is what God has to say to people . So the text of a sermon is like the recipe for a dish. A good cook would never be so focused on a recipe that she did not stop to realize that this was not at all the type of food her guests would need or appreciate. She would have her guests in mind from the start. After all, the goal of a good cook is not simply a matter of a recipe or a certain dish. It is feeding and feasting people . People drive the sermon. People are the reason God has given us the message in the biblical text. The biblical text leads the preacher to what the people need to hear from God. But the biblical text is only a means . The goal is people—to bring them somewhere that God wants them to go. To enlighten them, change them, help them, console them, correct them, train them to worship and serve God. People-oriented preaching comes from a God-centred, loving interest in them . Text-oriented preaching may simply come from the preacher’s love for preaching, for exegesis or for theology. A physician may be fascinated by medical treatments. But the good physician’s real interest is not treatments but people whose suffering has called for those treatments. Just so, true preaching is about people. That brings me to a second, related thought. We are often told that in preparing a sermon the key is finding the main idea of the text. To consider this as the key is not a people-oriented point of view and does not produce good preaching. It produces preaching with lots of emphasis on ideas and little emphasis on application. The key to preparing a sermon is not to find the main idea of the text. It is to find the main goal of the text. Not ‘What does the biblical text mainly say?’ But rather ‘What does this text intend to mainly do for people?’ What does the text intend mainly to effect in the lives of people? What does this text aim to move the people to believe, to do, to become? Application! A. T. Pierson, i
content_zh: 以下信件发表于"班纳杂志"2025年12月号. 它应一位读者的要求在这里出版,他觉得它很有帮助,希望它的律师也能得到他人的祝福。 也可以在"班纳·波德克特"上收听对这封信的读取. 亲爱的J-,在我们讨论申请布道后,我想,我将提出一些多年来我对这一问题的看法。 我想指出一些陷阱 你可能想记住 当你训练R. 我了解他们的唯一原因 就是自己花太多时间在他们身上 多年来,我一直以来都在自责自悔。 第一种想法是,太多时候(即使在一些关于布道的好书中),我们听到文字驱动布道. 这是半个事实。 一个潜在的危险 半真相。 我见过一个男人如此有意地公开他的文字(他做得非常好),他似乎没有注意到或关心房间里有三分之一的人在他完成布道之前就离开,因为他走了这么长一段时间,会议的最后一餐是用来应付当地火车时间的限制。 错误地注重案文及其解释会使我们忘记案文所要为的人。 一位挺身而出进行传道的传道者,在一周里,他90%的布道准备时间都集中在圣经文本上,但是他没有充分意识到实际的传道内容。 在他们所著的"沿着路"(Letrys A. A. Carson)和"约翰·伍德布里奇"(John Woodbridge)一书中这样写道: 传福音的宣讲之所以如此之多,实在是无趣而无关紧要的一个主要原因是,传道人花费了大量的不相称的准备时间来解剖和提纲,在思考"上帝之道"是怎样去伤口和愈合(使用"霍西"的语言)时却很少考虑. 1个 故传道以人为事. 意义在于上帝要对人们说 他们的生活 讲道的文字是上帝要对人们说的话。 所以布道的文字就像菜谱。 一个好厨师永远也不会把注意力集中在一个配方上,以至于她不禁意识到这根本不是客人需要或欣赏的食物类型. 她一开始就想着她的客人 毕竟,一个好厨师的目标不仅仅是一个菜谱或某种菜肴的问题. 它在给人们提供食物和盛宴。 人们驱使布道。 人们是上帝给我们圣经文本中的信息的原因。 圣经文本将传道人引向人们需要从上帝那里听到的. 但圣经文本只是一个手段。 目标是人们,把他们带到上帝要他们去的地方去。 为了启蒙他们,改变他们,帮助他们,安慰他们,矫正他们,训练他们去崇拜并服务于上帝. 以人为中心的布道来自以上帝为中心, 以文字为取向的传道可能只是来自传道者对传道、开教或神学的热爱。 医生可能因治疗而着迷。 但好医生的真正兴趣不是治疗,而是那些遭受痛苦需要治疗的人。 所以,真正的传道是关于人的。 这让我想到另一个相关的想法。 我们经常被告知,在准备布道时,关键在于找到案文的主要想法。 将此视为关键不是以人民为导向的观点,也不产生好传道. 它产生许多强调思想的布道,很少强调应用。 准备布道的关键不是找到文本的主要想法. 它是为了找到案文的主要目标。 而非"圣经主要说些什么?" 但更确切地说,“这个文本主要是为了什么?” 案文主要打算如何影响人们的生活? 这个文字的目的是要促使人们相信,去做,变成什么? 申请! A. T. 皮尔逊,i

summary_zh: 我们都需要对上帝对所有众生和事件的主权统治有更大的敏感性。亚历山大·卡森（ Alexander Carson ）的研究《圣经所体现的天意的历史》（ The History of Providence as Manifested in Scripture ）可以帮助我们培养这种敏感性。以下是耶利米书第14章中他对犹大饥荒主题的评论：由于饥荒的存在， […]犹大的饥荒后：上帝的普罗维登斯显示首先出现在美国真理的旗帜上。
title_zh: 犹大饥荒：神的普罗维登斯显现
content: We all need a greater sensitivity to God’s sovereign rule over all beings and events. Alexander Carson’s study, The History of Providence as Manifested in Scripture can help train us in such sensitivity. Here are his comments on the subject of famine in Judah from Jeremiah 14: FOR the existence of plenty as of famine, the wisdom of this world looks no higher than to what are called second causes. God, it is considered, is no farther concerned in these matters than as the author of certain general laws. He has set the machine a-going, and it continues to work by its own construction, without any regulation of a superintending hand. Climate, soil, cultivation, need, it is confessed, favourable seasons, but any divine direction of weather is supposed to be unnecessary. Timely rain—or the want of it, is a matter below the attention of the Ruler of the world. The blight and the mildew, the wet and the caterpillar, are enemies with which the farmer is to struggle; but they are never considered as armies of devastation sent into the fields by a righteous Providence. The history of the Old Testament gives us a key to Providence in the production of famine or of plenty. God regulates the supplies of the children of men as exactly as if each individual of the human race had his rations assigned him by the angels of heaven every rising sun: ‘The word of the Lord that came to Jeremiah concerning the dearth. Judah mourneth, and the gates thereof languish; they are black unto the ground; and the cry of Jerusalem is gone up. And their nobles have sent their little ones to the waters: they came to the pits, and found no water; they returned with their vessels empty: they were ashamed and confounded, and covered their heads. Because the ground is chapt, for there was no rain in the earth, the ploughmen were ashamed, they covered their heads. Yea, the hind also calved in the field, and forsook it, because there was no grass. And the wild asses did stand in the high places, they snuffed up the wind like dragons; their eyes did fail, because there was no grass. O Lord, though our iniquities testify against us, do thou it for thy name’s sake: for our backslidings are many; we have sinned against thee.’—Jer. 14:1–7. As in creation and in Providence, so in redemption, God hides himself in the midst of a blaze of light. In all his works he reveals himself, yet the enmity of the human heart will not allow men to see him. And what is most strange, the savage sees a divine hand in the works of Providence; it is unseen and denied by philosophical wisdom. The illiterate peasant hears God in his voice of thunder and storms, and acknowledges divine wrath in pestilence, sword, and famine. But the philosopher perceives nothing in all these but the course of nature. The wisdom of man makes itself ignorant of what the very beasts seem to feel. content_zh: 我们都需要更加关注上帝对所有生命和事件的主权统治。 Alexander Carson的研究, 《普罗维登斯的历史》, 以下是他从耶利米14号对犹大饥荒主题的评论: 对于饥荒时存在的富足,这个世界的智慧看起来并不比所谓的"第二原因"更高. 据认为,与某些一般法律的制定者相比,上帝在这些事务上没有更多的关切。 他把机器设为正常运行,它继续按自己的构造运作,没有任何管制的上司手. 气候,土壤,种植,需要,是承认的,有利的季节,但是任何神圣的天气方向都应该是不必要的. 及时降雨——或者说,这是世界统治者不关心的问题。 荒凉和温和的、湿润的和毛毛的,是农民要与之斗争的敌人;但他们从未被视为正义的普罗维登斯派入田地的毁灭军队。 "旧约"的历史为我们提供了普罗维登斯产生饥荒或富饶的关键. 真主为世人的给养而加以管理,犹如每个人的给养,每逢太阳升起,就奉天天神所赐给每个人一样。 犹大哀悼而其中的城门枯萎;他们已变成黑色的;耶路撒冷的呼声已升起。 其贵人又将小人送入水中去:来入坑中去,又无取出水来;又以器物入空而回;自惭而自愧,自蒙而出. 因为地是分明的,因为地上没有下雨,犁地人感到羞愧,就把头盖了起来. 有之,后人又以地为牛,而弃之,因有草而去. 野驴们的确站在高处,他们像龙一样把风扑倒;他们的眼睛确实衰败了,因为没有草. 主啊!我们的罪过虽能证明我们的罪过,但求你为你的名字而行之;我们的背负是多的;我们确已犯罪了。 与创造和普罗维登斯一样,在救赎中,上帝将自己隐藏在一束光芒中. 在他的所有作品中,他都暴露了自己,然而人心的敌意却不允许人见到他. 最奇怪的是,野蛮人看到普罗维登斯的作品中有神之手;它是看不见的,被哲学智慧所否定. 文盲农民在雷和风暴中听到上帝的声音,在瘟疫、剑和饥荒中承认神圣的愤怒。 但是哲学家在所有这些事物中,除了自然的走向,什么也看不出来. 人类的智慧使自己对野兽的感受一无所知. 更多信息:卡森所著"普罗维登斯的历史"(The History of Providence As Expressed in Books by Carson, Alexander price from: $ 13.50 学习更多选择选项描述) 基督教徒最感兴趣的话题。 以天经为阅读者,并举出真主赐予信士们的慰藉。 264pp. Featured Photo(当作品在社交媒体上分享时可以看见),

title_zh: 让苦涩的东西变甜的上帝
content: The Israelites had just walked between the walls of the water of the Red Sea and watched as the Lord washed away the whole Egyptian army. They sang a song of triumph on the far shore of the sea, rejoicing in the fear that had fallen on the surrounding nations (Ex. 15:14-16) and looking forward to taking possession of the Promised Land in the near future (Ex. 15:17). But within three days they raised a very different kind of sound—a chorus of grumbling against Moses because there was no water to drink at Marah (Ex. 15:22-26). I wonder what they expected would happen after the Red Sea. A straight, unhindered journey to the land flowing with milk and honey? Instead the first thing the Lord does is to lead his people to the undrinkable water of Marah. There is no question that the Lord is the one who led them there—it is easy enough to take a wrong turn when you are following Google Maps, but not when you are following a towering pillar of cloud or fire! So why did God lead Israel to Marah? Is it because he is sadistic and cruel and takes delight in watching his people suffer dehydration and fear? Is it because he is really bad at geography? Of course not! In fact we’re told why he brought Israel to Marah in Ex. 15:25: There the Lord tested them. In fact, the whole wilderness is a place of testing. That’s the significance of the wilderness—it’s a hard place. Deuteronomy 8:15 calls it ‘the vast and dreadful wilderness, that thirsty and waterless land, with its venomous snakes and scorpions.’ God is training his infant son to trust him—and training is always painful. There are no short cuts, whether in the physical training of our bodies to make them stronger and faster, or in the mental training of our minds to increase our knowledge and understanding, or in the spiritual training of our souls to grow in godliness. Learning to trust God is not something we can do lounging on the sofa. It means being put into situations that are stressful, confusing, messy and complicated, when we don’t understand what is going on or see any answers. Anyone can trust God when things are easy; the real test is if you will trust God when things are tough. Israel’s failure Marah was Israel’s first test and they failed. They have been travelling for three days and haven’t found any water. Supplies are running low. Perhaps as they saw the waters of Marah in the distance they finished up their last reserves: ‘It’ll be OK—we can refill very soon!’ Imagine the relief and joy as the first to reach Marah fall down and scoop the water to their mouths. And imagine them spitting it out as they discover it is foul and undrinkable. They’re not just disappointed—they’re horrified . Panic seizes them. ‘What shall we drink?’ (v. 24) This is not like someone in a restaurant complaining that their steak is a bit on the tough side or that the soup is a tad cold. They are exhausted and dehydrated and they can’t see any way of getting water. Suddenly life is hanging by a thread. There is nothing unreasonable about their concern. That is not why they fail the test. They fail the test because of their attitude. They grumble: the word means ‘hostile complaining, verbal attacks of dissatisfied people.’ Why do they grumble? There are at least two reasons: Faithlessness . They do not trust God. They don’t trust his power (that he can take care of them) or his goodness (that he wants to take care of them). They should have gone to the Lord with their needs, humbly asking him to provide what they needed. And this lack of faith was due to… Forgetfulness . This is the diagnosis of Psalm 78:40ff: How often they rebelled against him in the wilderness and grieved him in the desert! … They did not remember his power or the day when he redeemed them from the foe , 43 when he performed his signs in Egypt and his marvels in the fields of Zoan. The people had such short memories! It has only been three days since they walked through the Red Sea! It has been just a few weeks since they witn
content_zh: 以色列人刚刚走入了红海的水墙之间,看着上帝冲走整个埃及军队。 他们在远海岸上唱了一首"胜利之歌",欣喜地感受到了降临于周边民族的恐惧(Ex. 15:14-16)并期待着在不久的将来占有所承诺之地(Ex. 15:17). 但他们在三日内,举出一种非常不同的声音,一种对穆萨抱怨的合唱,因为在马拉没有水可饮(前15:22-26). 不知道红海之后他们会怎样 直走无阻地去 充满牛奶和蜂蜜的土地? 取而代之的是,主所行之事,是引其民入于马拉所出不可饮之水也. 毫无疑问,主是带领他们到那里去的——当你遵循Google地图时,很容易错转,但当你遵循高耸起的云柱或火柱时,就不是了! 那么为什么上帝带领以色列找到马拉? 是不是因为他是虐待狂和残忍的,在看着他的人民遭受脱水和恐惧时感到愉快? 是不是因为他在地理上很不好? 当然不是! 事实上我们被告知他为何在前15:25将以色列带到马拉:上帝在那里测试过他们。 事实上,整个荒地都是试验地. 这是荒野的意义, 8: 15 脱胎手术称之为:"大而可怕的荒野, 渴而无水之地, 有毒蛇和蝎子. 真主正在训练他的儿子,以便他信任他。训练确是痛苦的。 无论是身体锻炼,使其更强而更快,还是心灵修炼,以增进我们的知识和理解,或是心灵修炼,以在教化中成长,都没有任何短短的削减. 学会相信上帝不是我们能在沙发上做的事 这表示当我们不明白发生了什么情况或看到答案时, 当事情变得容易的时候,任何人都可以信任真主;真正的考验是,如果事情变得艰难的时候,你们要信任真主的话。 以色列的失败马拉是以色列的第一个考验, 他们已经旅行了三天, 补给不足。 也许当他们看到马拉的海水, 想象一下,解脱和欢乐是第一个到达马拉的人倒下,把水灌入口中. 想象一下他们发现它肮脏而不可饮用时就吐出它. 他们不仅失望, 恐慌抓住他们。 我们喝什么? (v.24) 这不像餐馆里有人抱怨 他们的牛排有点硬 或者汤有点冷 他们已经精疲力竭并脱水, 突然间,生命被一丝一缕地挂起 他们的关切没有什么不合理的。 这并不是他们失败的原因。 他们因为态度而未能通过测试. 他们抱怨道:这个词的意思是“敌意抱怨, 他们为什么抱怨? 至少有两个原因:失信。 他们不相信上帝。 他们不相信他的能力(他能照顾他们)或善良(他想照顾他们), 他们应该带着自己的需要去主那里,谦卑地要求他提供他们需要的东西. 缺乏信心是因为... 这就是对"诗经"78:40ff的诊断:他们在荒野中频繁地反抗他,在沙漠中为他悲伤!...... 他们不记得他的威力,也不记得他从敌人手中赎回他们的那一天,43岁时他在埃及行过他的迹象,他在Zoan地上行过他的奇事。 人们记忆很短! 他们从红海走过才三天! 几周前他们才开始

summary_zh: 费丝·库克（ Faith Cook ）的《麻烦之旅》（ Troubled Journey ）讲述了她作为OMF中国传教士的女儿的早期经历。为了表彰父母的信仰、勇气和自我牺牲，她还富有同情心地揭示了与父母长期分离所带来的家庭剥夺。下面的摘录是该书的第11章，其中[…]邮政父母：传教士儿童的经历首先出现在美国真理旗帜上。
title_zh: 邮政父母：传教士儿童的经历
content: Faith Cook’s Troubled Journey narrates her early experiences as the daughter of OMF missionaries to China. Honouring the faith, courage, and self-sacrifice of her parents, she also shines a compassionate light on the family deprivations brought about by long periods of separation from them. The excerpt below is Chapter 11 of the book in question, which cover Faith’s childhood between the ages of fourteen and eighteen. A passage on the P & O Carthage was booked for Stanley and Norah [Faith’s parents—Ed.] in early January 1952, only eight months after our family had first arrived back from China. It was a subdued Christmas we spent together that year, the last for some years to come. Frantic packing followed, purchasing school uniform and preparing for the long outward journey back to the Far East, this time by sea. A round of speaking engagements filled the days for my parents and seemingly eased the ache of the forthcoming separation. As the day of parting drew ever nearer, I noticed a new tenderness in their attitude towards me – a tenderness that only added to my distress. And at last came the day of departure. It would be four years before we would see them again. Photographs were taken on the steps of the mission headquarters, as all joined to wish the departing missionaries well. Norah’s expression told a story, as did fifteen-year-old Christopher’s forced smile, for in reality, the boy’s spirit was at breaking point. On we went to the station where our parents would board a train to Southampton. A large contingent of missionary personnel followed, for this departure was highly significant for the entire future of the mission, urgently seeking a new role for its operations now the door to China was closed. I found myself thrust to the back of the crowd as the train slowly moved off. Suddenly one more thoughtful friend spotted the irony of the situation and pushed me to the front to catch the last glimpse of my parents as they stood waving at the window of the train, my mother looking tense and tearful, and my father strained. Back at the mission home once more, we were at a loose end. No guardian had yet been appointed to care for us, although one or two kindly adults helped out if I asked for assistance. The Spring term would soon begin and I was glad. Some of my new clothes were too long and needed altering, and I discovered with alarm that the shoe repairer considered my school shoes beyond his skills to patch up. Never handy with a needle, I tried my best to turn up the hems myself. At last the third week of January arrived and I was on the train back to my well-loved school – a place I now regarded as home. Although soon immersed once more in all the trivia of boarding school life, I found time each week to write a letter to my parents. The first few letters were addressed to ports en route for Malaysia where the P & O Carthage would call: Aden, Penang and then to Singapore to await their arrival. Stanley and Norah treasured these schoolgirl epistles, storing them all up, until at last my father would present his married daughter with a shoe box crammed with letters dating from January 1952 until the time that he and my mother finally retired from missionary service in Malaysia more than twenty years later. These letters form a unique commentary on the development of a postal relationship with my parents that would form the bedrock of my security and development from a young teenager to womanhood and beyond. Faithfully my parents replied to each letter, commenting on my progress, chiding when they could sense my behaviour was becoming erratic, and offering advice as well as they were able. Not long after arriving back at the mission headquarters in London at the end of the spring school term, I discovered that a middle-aged couple had been appointed as guardians for the children of the missionaries: Louis and Nancy Gaussen. Understanding and kindly, they were well-suited to care for the children. ‘Mr and Mrs Gaussen
content_zh: Faith Cook的"麻烦之旅"讲述了她作为OMF传教士去中国的女儿的早期经历. 她以对父母的信仰、勇气和自我牺牲的敬意,也为长期与父母分离所带来的家庭贫困而发出同情之光。 下面的节录是该书第11章,其中涵盖了费斯14至18岁的童年. 1952年1月初,我们一家刚从中国回来才八个月,为斯坦利和诺拉(Faith的父母——Ed.)预订了P & O迦太基号上的一段。 那年是我们一起度过的圣诞 几年来的最后一天 紧随其后的弗朗克包装,购买了校服并准备了远东的漫长出行旅程,这次是海上出行. 一轮的演讲为我父母提供了时间,似乎缓解了即将到来的分居的痛苦。 随着离别日的临近,我注意到他们对我的态度出现了新的温柔,这种温柔只会使我更加痛苦。 终于到了出发之日 四年后我们才能再见到他们 对特派团总部的步骤进行了拍照,因为所有人都希望离开的传教士们一切顺利。 Norah的言论讲述了一个故事,15岁的Christopher被迫微笑也讲述了一个故事,因为实际上,这名男孩的精神正在崩溃。 我们去了车站 在那里,我们的父母 会登上火车到南安普顿。 随即派出了大批传教人员,因为这次出走对传教团的整个未来都具有重大意义,因此紧急寻求为传教团的行动起新的作用,现在中国的大门已经关闭了。 我发现自己被推倒 在人群的后部 当火车慢慢地离开。 突然又有一位深思熟虑的朋友发现情况具有讽刺意味,把我推到前面,以抓住我父母站在火车窗前挥手的最后一眼,我母亲看起来紧张而泪流满面,而我父亲也感到紧张. 回到了任务之家, 我们处在一个松散的结局。 目前还没有指定监护人来照顾我们,不过,如果我想得到帮助,一两个成年人会帮助我们。 春季学期即将开始 我很高兴 一些我的新衣服太长,需要更换,我惊恐地发现,修鞋者认为我的校鞋超出了他的能力来补补补. 我从不用针指手画脚,我尽力自己把螺丝弄大 终于在一月的第三个星期抵达, 我坐上火车回到我深爱的学校, 虽然我很快再次沉浸在寄宿学校生活的三难之中,但我发现每周都有时间写信给我的父母。 最初的几封信是寄给前往马来西亚的港口,P&O迦太基会称这些港口为:亚丁,槟城,再到新加坡等他们到达. 斯坦利和诺拉珍藏了这些女学生的表皮, 把它们全部储存起来, 直到最后我父亲会向他的已婚女儿展示一个鞋盒, 里面塞有1952年1月的信件, 直到他和我妈妈20多年后终于从马来西亚的传教士退休。 这些信件构成了关于与我父母发展邮政关系的独特评论,这将构成我从青少年到妇女时代及以后的安全和发展的基石。 诚然,我的父母每一封信都回信,评论我的进展,当他们能感觉到我的行为变得不规则时,他们就会发号施令,并尽可能地提供建议。 在春季学期结束回到伦敦的使团总部不久后,我发现一对中年夫妇被指定为传教士子女监护人:路易和南希·高森. 理解和友善,他们很适合照顾孩子。 高森夫妇

Some teaching on the Christian life asserts that […]   The post  In the Christian Life There is No Necessary Crisis Experience  appeared first on  Banner of Truth USA .
summary_zh: 六个帖子中的第四个帖子包含了阿尔伯特· N ·马丁（ Albert N. Martin ）在1984年旗帜青年大会（ Banner Youth Conference ）上给出的教学内容，展示了基督教生活的基本圣经神学。在基督徒的生活中，没有承诺或命令的危机经历是必不可少的元素。一些关于基督徒生活的教导断言， […]《基督徒生活中没有必要的危机经历》一文首先出现在《美国真理旗帜》上。
title_zh: 在基督徒的生活中，没有必要的危机经历
content: The fourth of six posts containing the substance of teaching given by Albert N. Martin at the 1984 Banner Youth Conference, presenting a basic biblical theology of the Christian life. There is no crisis experience promised or commanded as an essential element in living the Christian life. Some teaching on the Christian life asserts that only a low level of Christian experience can be realized by the person who has not had a crisis experience subsequent to regeneration, or at least subsequent to conversion and to the beginning of conscious Christian experience. Furthermore, it is asserted that the crisis experience is both commanded and promised by God as the entrance into a qualitatively new dimension or level of spiritual experience, reality and power. Throughout the history of the Christian church there have been many different strands of this crisis teaching. There is what we might call ‘classic Wesleyan perfectionism,’ which concentrated particularly upon sanctification and spoke of a baptism of purifying fire, or of coming into a state of perfect love. It concentrated not so much on power for service or upon inward feelings, but on a crisis experience in which the power of indwelling sin was to all intents and purposes negated. I have read enough of classic Wesleyan theology to know that there are different opinions as to what John Wesley himself taught on the subject. But in a general descriptive manner this, I believe, is an accurate representation of old-style classic Wesleyan perfectionism. Then, too, there is ‘the old Pentecostalism’ in which the emphasis was upon a baptism in the Holy Spirit, generally subsequent to conversion, and invariably manifested by speaking in tongues: the way you knew that you had this baptism of power was that, when it came to you, you spoke in tongues. The primary focus in old classic Pentecostalism was the matter of power for service. Thirdly, there is the modern ‘charismatic movement.’ Like classic Pentecostalism, its teachers use many of the same passages in the Book of Acts to support their theory of this necessary crisis. So they emphasize that in most cases—although there are different schools among modern charismatics—it will be manifested by the speaking in tongues. Some are content to believe you have ‘got it’ if you have a season of holy laughter. Others, however, say that you have not spoken in tongues because you have some psychological hold-ups, and if these can be removed the tongues are there. You just have not given them utterance. Here the emphasis is not so much on a baptism of purifying fire (as in the case of old classic Wesleyan perfectionism), or the baptism of power (as in the case of old classic Pentecostalism), but more upon a baptism of joyful praise-filled experience. I have been speaking of generalities, but I believe they are accurate. Fourthly, there are the various forms of ‘higher life’ teaching. What they have in common is this: you are simply converted, simply united to Christ, simply regenerated, and then you come to a crisis of surrender and faith, in which ‘you let go and let God’ and appropriate the indwelling life of Christ. The common denominator is that it is a crisis without any external manifestation of tongues or holy laughter or shouting or jumping, but the end result will be new power to live a holy life—the emphasis falls upon the ability to be more efficient in the path of holiness. Fifthly, there is a kind of teaching which has both old and modern proponents. It focuses on assurance, and has been expressed in terms of the biblical language of a ‘sealing of the Holy Spirit.’ Some of the Puritans—Thomas Goodwin, for example—taught this. There have been certain preachers in our own day who have believed this very strongly and emphasized it repeatedly. The basic concern in this teaching is that, subsequent to regeneration and conversion, there is a crisis experience in which the believer enters into a qualitatively new dimension of assurance by
content_zh: 阿尔伯特·N·马丁在1984年班纳青年会议上发表的包含教学内容的六篇文章中的第四篇,介绍了基督教生活的基本圣经神学. 没有任何危机经历作为过上基督教生活的一项基本要素得到承诺或接受。 一些关于基督教生活的教义主张,在再生后,或至少是在皈依后,以及自觉的基督教经历开始后,没有危机经历的人,只有低水平的基督教经验才能实现. 此外,有人断言,危机经历既是上帝的旨意,也是上帝的允诺,是精神经历、现实和力量进入一个全新的层面或层次的。 在基督教会的历史上,这种危机教育有许多不同的内容。 我们可能称之为“经典的卫斯理完美主义 ” , 它不是把精力集中在服务或内在感情上,而是集中在一种危机经历上,在这种经历中,罪恶的威力是所有意图和目的所否定的。 我读了足够多的经典的卫斯理神学,知道对于约翰·卫斯理自己教授的这个主题,有不同的看法. 但从一般的描述方式来看,我认为,这是对老式经典的卫斯理主义的准确表述. 也存在“五旬节派”的旧现象, 重点是圣灵中的洗礼, 通常是在皈依之后, 古老的经典五旬节主义的主要焦点是服务的权力问题. 第三,有现代`魅力运动'。 和经典的五旬节主义一样,它的老师们也用"行动书"中的许多同名段落来支持他们对这个必要危机的理论. 所以他们强调,在多数情况下,尽管现代魅力中存在着不同的学校,但用舌头说话将表明这一点。 如果你有一个圣笑的季节, 然而,其他人说,你没有说出舌头,因为你有一些心理障碍,如果这些障碍可以取出,舌头就在那里。 你只是没说 这里强调的不是净化火的洗礼(如旧经典的卫斯理完美主义),也不是权力的洗礼(如旧经典的五旬节主义),而是更强调充满欢乐的赞美经验的洗礼. 我一直在谈论泛泛而谈,但我认为它们是正确的。 第四,有各种形式的 " 更高的生活 " 教学。 他们的共同点是:你们只是皈依正教,只是与基督联合,只是再生,然后你们遭遇了投降和信仰的危机,你们在危机中“放手,放任真主出征”,而顺从基督永生。 共同的分母是,这是一场没有外在表现出舌头或圣笑或叫喊或跳跃的危机,但最终结果将是新的力量来过上圣生活——强调在圣道上更有效率的能力. 第五,有一种教学既有老的也有现代的支持者。 它侧重于保证,并用圣经中的"封圣"来表述. 一些清教徒——例如托马斯·古德温——教授了这个。 在我们这一天里,有一些传道者非常强烈地相信并反复强调这一点。 该教学的基本关注是,在再生和转生之后,存在着一种危机经历,信仰者通过下列方式进入了保证的质的新层面:

What follows is Chapter 4 of that title, ‘Hard Days and Golden Years.’ If there was any pattern to Amy Carmichael’s life it was of times of refreshing then of trials, of exhilarating ‘climbing’ […]   The post  Amy Carmichael: Times of Refreshing and Times of Trial  appeared first on  Banner of Truth USA .
summary_zh: 伊恩· H ·穆雷（ Iain H. Murray ）的《艾米·卡迈克尔：灰烬之美》（ Amy Carmichael: Beauty for Ashes ）是对爱尔兰传教士前往印度的非凡生活的简短复述。接下来是该标题的第4章， “艰难的日子和黄金岁月。“如果说艾米·卡迈克尔的生活有任何模式的话，那就是令人耳目一新的时代，然后是考验的时代，令人兴奋的‘攀登’的时代[…]艾米·卡迈克尔的帖子：令人耳目一新的时代和考验的时代首先出现在真理美国的旗帜上。
title_zh: 艾米·卡迈克尔：令人耳目一新的时代和审判的时代
content: Iain H. Murray’s Amy Carmichael: Beauty for Ashes is a short retelling of the remarkable life of the Irish missionary to India. What follows is Chapter 4 of that title, ‘Hard Days and Golden Years.’ If there was any pattern to Amy Carmichael’s life it was of times of refreshing then of trials, of exhilarating ‘climbing’ then of walking in dark ravines. In part her explanation was that demonic activity follows the work of the Holy Spirit. As she quoted from George Bowen, When Christianity assumes an aggressive attitude the first result is a great exhibition of Satanic power. Satan’s power to be manifested must be assaulted. 1 Such an understanding does not come so readily to us who do not live, as she did, within sight of demon possession, or within hearing of tom-tom drums calling devotees to idols. Shortly before Walker 2 had left on his last mission, he had been sitting with Amy and others in deck chairs under the stars. ‘We had been talking’, she later wrote, of work and workers, and of those (to me) most wonderful women, who seemed perfectly self-reliant, needing no strong arm alongside. I remember how, suddenly startled at the bare thought of working alone, in the sense of all the burden of responsibility, I exclaimed that I never could do it. Mr Walker laughed. ‘Well, you don’t have to’, he said. 3 Amy was the weaker when her ‘strong arm’ died at the age of fifty-four. What she owed to Walker’s ‘courageous championship’ of the children’s work, ‘through its first very difficult years, no words can tell, nor can words tell how he is missed’. 4 At times, as she faced her loss, she would need to say to herself, ‘Don’t give up, don’t be afraid: go on.’ Prayer for ‘fortitude’ entered her life. There were unsympathetic neighbours who observed the work at Dohnavur who supposed that Amy would now be more vulnerable. One of these was a lawyer who, soon after Walker’s death, wrote with the demand that current work on the building of a wall around the compoundbe stopped, and that a half-built nursery should be pulled down. They were using ground, he claimed, to which they did not have legal title. ‘He had waited till Mr Walker’s death had left us, as he thought, defenceless, almost desolate, and sure to be easily cowed by threats of court trouble.’ The wall building had been prompted by the passage of a tiger through the compound at night; and the new nursery was necessitated by the growing numbers of children for whom Dohnavur had become home. Amy ignored the letter and heard nothing more of the threat. The Dohnavur family of seventy children and grown-ups in 1906, had doubled itself by this date, and the need of more helpers was pressing. Mrs Catherine Carmichael was never able to return. She died on July 14, 1913. A few weeks earlier a letter from her to Amy began with the words, ‘My own most precious earthly possession’. While Amy did not lament her mother’s death—for no Christian death was to be ‘lamented’—in the days ahead she needed to preach to herself, ‘I must remind myself to live in the joy of those gone, not grovel in the sense of my loss.’ Mrs Carmichael had been a constant supporter and representative for Dohnavur in Britain. She acted as the home secretary to whom gifts could be sent, and helped to make her daughter’s books more widely known. In 1912 those books had been noted by Queen Mary, wife of King George V, who expressed her thanks for them. While Amy was busy in 1913 writing Walker of Tinnevelly , there came the possibility of the loss of her closest female friend and helper, Ponnammal, who had been with her ever since, as a young widow, she had come to new life through Walker’s preaching. She now needed surgery for cancer and Amy went with her to a Salvation Army Hospital at Neyyoor for a period. In their absence from Dohnavur (forty-six miles away), and the absence of Mabel Wade who was on furlough, 70 of the children were ill. The need for more medical facilities at Dohnavur itself was evident. After much s
content_zh: 伊恩·H·默里所著的"艾米·卡迈克尔:爱希斯的美人"(Amy Carmichael: Beautiful for Ashes)是爱尔兰传教士到印度的出众生的短篇回忆. 下面是该标题的第4章: " 艰难的日子和黄金年 " 。 如果Amy Carmichael的生活有任何规律的话, 她的部分解释是,妖魔活动遵循了圣灵的工作. 正如她从乔治·博文所引述的那样,当基督教采取侵略态度时,第一个结果就是撒旦力量的伟大展览. 必须攻击撒旦的力量。 1 对我们来说,这种理解并不像她那样活在恶魔拥有的目光下,或者在听到汤姆·通鼓呼唤献给偶像的人面前。 在行走者2号执行上个任务前不久,他一直和艾米等人坐在星空下的甲板椅上. 她后来写道:‘我们谈过了',内容是工作和工人,以及那些似乎完全自力更生、不需要任何坚强的手臂的妇女。 我记得,我突然对独自工作的赤裸裸的想法感到惊奇,因为我肩负着所有的责任,我感到惊叹,我永远做不到。 华克先生笑了 他说,你不必这么做。 3 Amy在54岁时死亡, 她对沃克的“勇敢的冠军”儿童工作所负的责任是,“在第一个非常困难的岁月里,言语无法分辨,言语也无法分辨他是如何被错过的”。 页:1 有时,当她面临损失时,她需要对自己说: " 不要放弃,不要害怕:继续吧。 " 祈求`宽恕'进入她的生活。 有不同情的邻居在多赫纳武尔观察作品,他们认为艾米现在会更加脆弱. 其中一个是一位律师,他在Walker死后不久写道,他要求停止目前在大院周围建造一堵墙的工作,应当拆除一个半建的托儿所。 他声称,他们使用了他们没有合法所有权的地盘。 他一直等待着沃克先生的死像他所想的那样离开我们,他手无寸铁,几乎是荒凉的,而且肯定很容易被法庭麻烦的威胁吓倒了。 墙上建筑的动因是一只老虎在夜间穿过大院;新的托儿所是因越来越多的儿童成为家而必需的。 艾米无视信件,没有听到更多的威胁. 1906年有70个孩子和成年人的多赫纳武尔家族,到这时已使自己翻了一番,迫切需要更多的帮助. 凯瑟琳·卡迈克尔夫人一直没能回来 她于1913年7月14日去世. 几周前,她给艾米的一封信开头写道,“我拥有自己最珍贵的地产”。 Amy没有为她母亲的死感到悲哀——因为没有一个基督徒的死是`在她需要为自己传道的几天里感到悲伤',`我必须提醒自己生活在那些死去的人的欢快中,而不是在我失去的意义上的忧郁'。 卡迈克尔夫人一直是英国多赫纳武尔的支持者和代表。 她担任家庭秘书,可以向她寄送礼物,并帮助使她女儿的书更广为人知。 1912年,这些书被乔治五世国王的妻子玛丽王后所注意到,玛丽王后对之表示感谢. 在1913年艾米忙于写作"Tinnevelly"的Walker(Walker of Tinnevelly)时,出现了失去她最亲密的女性朋友和助手Ponnammal(Ponnammal)的可能性,她从那时起就一直与她在一起,作为一个年轻的寡妇,她通过Walker的传道而来到了新的生活. 她现在需要手术治疗癌症,艾米和她一起去内约尔的救世军医院住了一段时间. 在他们离开多克纳武尔(相距四十六里外),而当时在放假的马贝尔·韦德(英语:Mabel Wade (film))不在的情况下,70个孩子生病了. Dohnavur本身显然需要更多的医疗设施。 这么多之后

content: An IMB missionary among the Deaf records a Bible story in sign language. IMB Photo Every dollar you give to the Lottie Moon offering goes to support missionaries like Noah Lewis who live and serve among the lost. Will you consider giving today? Noah Lewis couldn’t help signing along with a worship song playing in the background as Deaf friends gathered in his home for dinner. The International Mission Board appoints missionaries who are both Deaf and hearing to serve among the global Deaf. Many missionaries learn sign language for the first time, while others use their American Sign Language to more quickly learn global sign languages. IMB Photo The International Mission Board missionary was sitting in the living room with his roommate and two friends while others prepared food nearby. As a young, single adult, simply opening the doors to his home in the Middle East has created some of his most fruitful opportunities for gospel conversations. That evening, Lewis was stirred to worship the Lord. “I just love worshiping in sign language because it’s a full-body experience,” Lewis said. Lewis, who is hearing, began signing the song in American Sign Language. Across the room, one of his Muslim friends watched intently. When the song ended, his friend told him it was beautiful and asked to see another. Lewis explained that Christians use songs to worship God. His friend compared what he had seen to hearing the Islamic call to prayer. The exchange opened an opportunity for Lewis to explain Christian worship and why Christians worship Jesus. When his friend asked to see more, Lewis continued signing songs from the playlist. “He was just really captivated by it,” Lewis said. “It really felt like in that moment the Spirit was working in his heart.” The conversation did not end with a profession of faith. Instead, it became another step in a friendship where Lewis has watched spiritual curiosity grow over time. During Ramadan, the same friend asked about fasting. On another night, he asked how Christians pray. Each question has allowed Lewis to explain what Christians believe and why he follows Jesus. Those conversations reflect much of Lewis’ ministry. He has served in the Middle East for nearly a year and a half, spending much of his time learning sign language and building relationships in the local Deaf community. Learning sign language, like learning any language, requires time, practice and immersion in the community that uses it. For Lewis, that process has looked different from the experience of missionaries who can spend several hours each day in a formal language school. There are no comparable sign language centers where he serves, so much of his language learning happens through relationships with Deaf friends. Although Lewis has not had a dedicated language tutor since arriving on the field, personal relationships help him develop a strong conversational understanding of the sign language used where he serves. The process has also drawn him more deeply into the Deaf community he came to reach. “I want to genuinely learn about their language,” he said. “I want to be friends with them. I want to know who they are.” As Lewis’ ability to communicate grows, relationships deepen and opportunities to share the gospel follow. Even when he doesn’t know the exact sign he needs, friends help him find ways to communicate biblical truths. Lewis has learned to faithfully use the language he has while continuing to grow in his ability to communicate the gospel clearly. An IMB worker among the Deaf records a Bible story. Generous giving to the Lottie Moon Christmas Offering supports missions among the global Deaf. IMB Photo When the plan disappeared That dependence on God came into clearer focus during a recent trip to Central Asia. Lewis currently lives and serves in the Middle East, but he arrived on the field with a long-term desire to serve in Central Asia. 一名IMB在聋人中的传教士用手语记录圣经故事. IMB照片 你给洛蒂月球的每一美元 都用来支持传教士 比如诺亚·刘易斯 你会考虑今天给钱吗? 当聋人朋友聚集在家中吃饭时,

国际代表团委员会任命聋人和听力传教士在全球聋人中任职。 许多传教士首次学习手语,而其他传教士则使用他们的美国手语更快地学习全球手语.

IMB照片 国际传教委员会传教士与他的室友和两个朋友坐在客厅里,而其他人则在附近准备食物. 作为一个年轻、单身的成年人,只要打开通往他在中东的家的大门,就为他的福音对话创造了一些最富有成果的机会。 当晚,刘易斯被激起崇拜主.

「我只是喜欢手语崇拜, 正在听话的刘易斯开始用美国手语签署歌曲. 在房间里,他的一个穆斯林朋友故意观看。 歌曲结束的时候,他的朋友告诉他这很美丽,并请求见另一首. 刘易斯解释说,基督徒使用歌曲来崇拜上帝.

他的朋友比较了他所看到的听到的伊斯兰祈祷的呼声. 这次交流为刘易斯解释基督教崇拜和基督徒为何崇拜耶稣提供了机会. 当他的朋友要求看到更多时,刘易斯继续从播放列表上签名歌曲. 刘易斯说:“他只是被它迷住了。”

“在那个时刻,精神确实在他心中发挥作用。” 对话没有以信仰职业结束。 相反,它成为友谊的又一个步骤,刘易斯目睹了精神好奇心随时间推移而增长. 斋月期间,同友问斋事. 在另一个晚上,他问基督徒如何祈祷.

每个问题都让刘易斯解释基督徒相信什么,为什么他跟随耶稣. 这些谈话反映了刘易斯部的许多情况。 他在中东服务了近一年半,花了很多时间学习手语,在当地聋人社区建立关系.

学习手语,就像学习任何语言一样,需要时间,练习和沉浸在使用手语的社区中. 对刘易斯来说,这一进程与传教士的经历不同,传教士可以每天在一所正式语言学校中度过几个小时。

他所服务的手语中心并不存在类似的手语中心,所以他的许多语言学习都是通过与聋人朋友的关系发生的. 虽然刘易斯自到达球场后便没有专门的语言辅导员,但个人关系帮助他发展出对他所服务的手语的强烈的对话理解.

这一过程还使他更深入地融入了他所接触的聋人社区。 他说:“我想真正了解他们的语言。” “我想与他们成为朋友。 我想知道他们是谁。” 随着刘易斯沟通能力的增长,关系加深,分享福音的机会随之而来。

即使他不知道自己需要什么具体标志, 刘易斯学会了忠实使用他拥有的语言,同时继续增强他明确传达福音的能力. 一个IMB工人在聋人中记录了一个圣经故事. 慷慨地给洛蒂月亮圣诞节 提供全球聋人中的支持任务

title_zh: 俄亥俄州派遣庆祝活动确认33名IMB传教士为全球服务
content: Participants at the IMB Sending Celebration on Nov. 9, 2026, celebrated God's faithfulness in sending 33 new missionaries to the nations. Held at the Sugarcreek campus of First Baptist Kettering near Dayton, Ohio, the event launched the State Convention of Baptists in Ohio annual gathering. For security reasons, some newly appointed missionaries are not publicly identified. IMB Photo God continues to call His people to carry the gospel to the ends of the earth. During a Sending Celebration Nov. 9 at the Sugarcreek Campus of First Baptist Church Kettering, near Dayton, Ohio, 33 International Mission Board missionaries stood before family, friends and supporters, affirming their obedience to that call. Trustees of the IMB appointed the fully supported missionaries who represent 10 states – including two candidates from Ohio – and many Southern Baptist churches committed to sending and sustaining those called by God to go to the mission field. Senior Pastor Chad Keck welcomed those in attendance, sharing his appreciation for the partnership with Southern Baptist churches to cooperatively send and support missionaries. The Sending Celebration is meeting in conjunction with the State Convention of Baptists in Ohio. Chad Keck, senior pastor of First Baptist Kettering near Dayton, Ohio, left, and Jeremy Westbrook, executive director-treasurer of the State Convention of Baptists in Ohio, right, welcome guests gathered for the IMB Sending Celebration, which kicked off the convention’s annual gathering. IMB Photo Among those who shared their stories include a couple who answered an unexpected call later in life, a couple who are returning to Albania and to people they could not forget; and a couple who moved from welcoming the nations in Canada to going to Fiji. All of them shared their stories before the Sending Celebration. Unexpected invitation to go On Dec. 5, 2025, what seemed like an ordinary FaceTime call became a turning point for Rob Boss. As he spoke with his daughter, Hannah, during her IMB training, Rob sensed God speaking clearly to his heart: “You can do this too.” The impression was unexpected. After decades of writing, Christian education, seminary teaching and active support of missions, overseas service had never been part of Rob and Stephanie Boss’ plans. “It wasn’t an audible voice, but it was so clear,” Rob said. “It was Him. It was so kind and so gentle and so encouraging.” The moment drove him to his knees in surrender. When Stephanie came home later that day, he told her he believed God was calling them to the nations. Her response was immediate. “Thrilled is the right answer,” she said. The next day, the couple contacted the IMB and began the application process. Though missions had long been part of their family’s story, Rob and Stephanie Boss sensed God leading them to overseas service while encouraging their daughter, Hannah, during her missionary training. Sent by Wedgwood Baptist Church in Fort Worth, Texas, they are now headed to Colombia, where they will serve through theological education. IMB Photo Looking back, the Bosses see the Lord’s hand preparing them long before they realized where He was leading. “God brought us together in the summer of 1990 at Glorieta, New Mexico, where we met and married,” Stephanie said during the Sending Celebration. What followed was years of ministry, teaching, parenting and navigating life’s unexpected turns, which taught them to hold plans loosely and trust God completely. “We did not have a clue about what life held in front of us,” Stephanie said. “We just knew we wanted to follow the Lord.” Their calling also continues a family legacy. Rob’s mother served with the IMB in Africa after retirement, helping inspire Hannah’s service in South Korea. Now, three generations of the same family have answered God’s call to the nations. Rob and Stephanie expressed deep gratitude for their sending church, Wedgwood Baptist Church in Fort Worth, whose strong commitment to missions

2026年11月9日的IMB送信庆典的参与者,庆祝上帝向各国派遣33名新传教士的忠诚. 该活动在俄亥俄州代顿附近的第一浸信会Kettling的Sugarcreek校园举行,在俄亥俄州发起了浸信会州议会年会。 出于安全考虑,一些新任命的传教士没有公开身份.

IMB图片神继续呼叫 他的族人将福音传到地底 11月9日,在俄亥俄州代顿附近的第一浸信会Kettling教堂的Sugarcreek校区,33名国际传教委员会传教士站在家人、朋友和支持者面前,申明他们服从这一呼吁。

IMB的受托人任命了代表10个州的全力支持的传教士 — — 包括俄亥俄州的两名候选人 — — 以及许多南方浸信会教会承诺将那些被上帝召唤去传教的传教士送去并维持下去.

高级牧师Chad Keck欢迎与会者,与他一样感谢与美南浸信会教会合作派遣和支持传教士。 送教庆典会与俄亥俄州的浸信会州会议同时举行.

俄亥俄州代顿附近第一浸信会Ketting的资深牧师查德·凯克(Chad Keck)左翼,俄亥俄州浸信会执行董事兼创始人杰里米·韦斯特布鲁克(Jeremy Westbrook)右翼欢迎前来参加IMB送信庆典的来宾,这驱散了大会的年度集会。

在分享自己故事的人中,有一对夫妇在生活后期意外地接了电话,一对夫妇正在返回阿尔巴尼亚,一对夫妇无法忘记;一对夫妇从欢迎加拿大各国搬到斐济。 他们都分享了他们的故事 在送信庆典之前。 意外邀请 Dec 上。

5, 2025, 看起来像一个普通的FaceTime电话成为Rob Boss的转折点. 当他和他的女儿汉娜在IMB训练期间交谈时,罗布感应到上帝对他说的很清楚:“你也可以这样做。” 印象出乎意料。

经过几十年的写作、基督教教育、神学院教学和对使团的积极支持,海外服务从未成为罗布和斯蒂芬妮·博斯计划的一部分。 Rob说, “这不是一个声音, “这是他。 它是如此善良和温柔,如此鼓舞人心。” 那一刻,他被迫跪在地上投降。

当斯蒂芬妮当天晚些时候回家时,他告诉她,他相信上帝在召唤他们到各国. 她立即作出反应。 她说,“令人惊叹的是正确的答案。” 次日,夫妇联系IMB,开始了申请程序.

虽然传教团早就是他们家庭故事的一部分,但罗布和史蒂芬妮·博斯感知到,在传教团训练期间,他们带领他们到海外服务,同时鼓励他们的女儿汉娜。 由德克萨斯州沃思堡的韦奇伍德浸信会(Wedgwood Baptist Church)派遣,他们现在前往哥伦比亚,通过神学教育服务.

IMB照片回想起来,老板们看到主的手 在他们意识到在哪里之前很早就准备了 他是领导。 " 1990年夏天,上帝把我们带到了新墨西哥州格洛里埃塔,我们在那里相遇并结婚。 " Stephanie在送货庆典上说。

接下来是多年的教职、教职、养育和过着意想不到的转折,教他们松动计划,完全相信上帝。 Stephanie说:“我们不知道我们面前的生活是什么。” 我们只知道我们想跟随主。 他们的召唤也延续了家庭遗产。

罗布的母亲退休后在非洲为IMB效力,帮助激励汉娜在韩国服役. 现在,同一家庭的三代人响应了上帝向各国发出的呼吁。 Rob和Stephanie深表感谢他们派来的教会Worth堡的Wedgwood浸信会教堂,他们坚定致力于使命

content: A Senegalese Christian shares the gospel with event volunteers during the Youth Olympic Games in Dakar. IMB Photo As athletes and spectators from around the world fill the streets of Senegal for the Dakar 2026 Youth Olympic Games, missionaries and local believers are praying the event will leave behind more than medals and memories. For Carson West, an International Mission Board missionary serving in Senegal, the Games represent a unique opportunity not only to engage visitors with the gospel but also to mobilize local churches to take a more active role in evangelism long after the Olympic flame is extinguished. “This is the first Olympic event ever held on the continent of Africa,” West said. “For us, it was an opportunity to ask, ‘What are we going to do with this?’” The Youth Olympic Games, which began Oct. 31 and end Nov. 13, are taking place across three host cities: Dakar, Diamniadio and Saly. Event organizers expect nearly 2,700 athletes, ages 14-17, to participate in 35 sports and represent more than 200 delegations. The Games have drawn a million spectators, and West reported more than 6,000 event volunteers are staffing all the venues. With so many people gathering in Senegal, West and his team concentrated on preparing Senegalese churches for evangelistic opportunities. “We could run and hide, or we could do this thing,” West said, recalling an early conversation with teammates. “We decided we were going to do this thing.” The 2026 Youth Olympic Games in Dakar, Senegal, is the first Olympic event held on the continent of Africa. IMB Photo West serves as team leader for IMB work in Senegal, where ministry efforts focus on three areas: gospel engagement, church advancement and community development. The Youth Olympic outreach naturally aligns with the first two priorities. “Our approach has been to mobilize the local church,” he said. “This is their backyard.” Instead of relying on a large influx of international volunteers, though there is one volunteer team from the United States serving, the strategy has centered on equipping local believers. Senegal has four Baptist churches in the greater Dakar area. Many leaders representing the congregations, as well as other ministry partners, participated in evangelism training designed specifically for the Games. Church leaders and ministry partners in Senegal participate in an evangelism training session specifically designed to share the gospel during the Youth Olympic Games in Dakar. IMB Photo A key outreach method involves trading commemorative pins, a familiar Olympic tradition. Volunteers use the exchange as a natural conversation starter before offering gospel-centered materials. Each pin is accompanied by a card featuring a QR code connected to a digital engagement platform adapted from previous Olympic and World Cup outreaches. Visitors who scan the code are directed to online resources and can connect with trained digital responders. Experienced volunteers in the U.S. are helping provide follow-up conversations. “We’re building on strategies that have been used effectively in previous Olympic Games,” West said. “It’s an easy, non-intimidating way to start gospel conversations.” Trading commemorative pins is an Olympic tradition. Volunteers use these pins to start gospel-driven conversations during the Youth Olympic Games in Dakar. Each pin is accompanied by a card featuring a QR code that connects people to trained digital responders. IMB Photo The effort extends beyond Dakar. IMB teams and church partners are positioned in each of the three host cities. An IMB team, which includes three global missionary partners, is helping coordinate outreach efforts in Diamniadio, and an IMB team along with a Baptist church is organizing efforts in Saly. West believes the greatest potential impact may be felt not among international visitors but among Senegalese believers themselves. Senegal is approximately 95% Muslim and 0.2% evangelical. title: IMB seeks teachers, healthcare workers, business professionals to serve as missionaries
summary: When most Southern Baptists think of missionaries, they often picture church planters and evangelists. But leaders with the International Mission Board say some of the greatest needs today are for professionals whose work happens behind the scenes. IMB leaders report that critical roles such as teachers, healthcare workers, counselors, accountants, logistics specialists and member care personnel are helping advance the Great Commission in ways many churches never see. Doreen Baker, IMB director

title_zh: IMB寻求教师、医护人员、商业专业人士担任传教士
content: IMB missionary Dr. Heidi Haun, left, checks on patients at Baptist Medical Centre in Nalerigu, Ghana. There are needed roles for IMB missionaries in healthcare, ministering to the needs of local populations and utilizing this time to minister to spiritual needs. IMB Photo When most Southern Baptists think of missionaries, they often picture church planters and evangelists. But leaders with the International Mission Board say some of the greatest needs today are for professionals whose work happens behind the scenes. IMB leaders report that critical roles such as teachers, healthcare workers, counselors, accountants, logistics specialists and member care personnel are helping advance the Great Commission in ways many churches never see. Doreen Baker, IMB director of TCK (third culture kid or missionary kid) education, sees a constant need for education professionals. Teachers are needed in international schools, which cover a variety of global educational entities, and in other settings to provide for missionary kids and their educational needs. “Teachers are significant in that not only are they providing instruction for students, but they are an integral part of the core missionary task ,” Baker said. “We also have great needs for consultants to support our families on the field with their children’s education in many ways.” Baker previously served 25 years teaching in Asia and experienced how education creates access to missions where traditional pathways may be limited. IMB missionary Ellie Bohrer teaches a 12th grade World Views class at Black Forest Academy in Germany. The IMB is seeking other educators, like Bohrer, who are willing to use their skills on the mission field. IMB Photo Scott Ray, IMB senior director of global deployment, noted that many missionary positions go unfilled simply because they fall outside traditional perceptions of missionary service. He said professional skills can provide both practical ministry support and access to countries where traditional missionary visas are difficult to obtain. Opportunities exist for finance professionals, veterinarians, medical workers, Send Relief personnel and others. Healthcare remains one of the most strategic areas in demand. Tom Hicks, IMB director of global health strategies, said many medical professionals have the wrong perception about mission work. “We do have an issue where people will select out because they don’t think that what they do is useful on the mission field,” he said. In reality, Hicks said many areas across the globe are increasingly seeking family medicine physicians, internists, pediatricians, pediatric nurse practitioners, OB providers, physical therapists, occupational therapists, speech pathologists and lactation consultants. The need is especially significant in sub-Saharan Africa, where young populations create a growing demand for pediatric care. Healthcare professionals also provide a unique advantage in countries that restrict missionary activity. “Missionaries with a vocational value, like healthcare missionaries, have opportunities to go places that others can’t go,” Hicks said. Another often-overlooked ministry is member care, which focuses on the spiritual, emotional, mental and relational health of IMB missionaries. Chris Martin is the IMB director of global member care. “Member care missionaries stand alongside those missionaries that are thought of traditionally as church planters or evangelists and support them,” Martin said. Many who serve in these roles come from counseling backgrounds and help missionaries navigate stress, conflict, grief and other challenges that can affect long-term ministry effectiveness. Martin compares their role to Aaron and Hur in Exodus 19, holding up Moses’ arms during battle, strengthening those serving on the front lines. IMB missionary Glen Garner uses his business skills and experience as the logistics director for missionaries serving globally. He lives in Lima, Peru, with his wife, Shannon
content_zh: IMB传教士海迪·哈恩博士出走,在加纳纳莱里古的浸信会医疗中心检查病人. 咨监委的传教士在保健、满足当地居民需要和利用这一时间满足精神需要方面需要发挥作用。 IMB Photo 当大多数"南方浸信会"想到传教士时,他们经常会描绘出教会的植树人和福音会信徒. 但国际使命委员会的领导人说,今天最需要的是那些在幕后工作的专业人员。 咨监委领导人报告说,教师、保健工作者、顾问、会计师、后勤专家和成员护理人员等关键角色正在帮助推进大委员会,许多教会从未看到过。 多琳·贝克(英语:Doreen Baker,IMB Director of TCK (TCK)教育(英语:TCK (third Culture kid or missionary kid)))的导演,不断看到教育专业人士的需求. 国际学校需要教师,这些学校包括各种全球教育实体,其他环境则需要教师,以满足传教儿童及其教育需要。 教师不仅为学生授课, 也是核心传教任务的组成部分。 " 我们还非常需要顾问,以多种方式支持我们在外地的家庭,教育他们的孩子。 " 贝克以前在亚洲执教了25年,并体验了教育如何创造进入传统途径可能有限的特派团的机会。 IMB传教士艾莉·波克勒在德国黑森林学院教授一门12年级"世界观"课程. IMB正在寻找其他教育者,比如波尔,他们愿意在任务领域运用自己的技能. IMB Photo Scott Ray是IMB全球部署的高级主任,他指出,许多传教士职位由于不属于传教士服务的传统观念而无人填补. 他说,专业技能既能提供实用的部委支助,也能进入传统传教签证难以获得的国家。 金融专业人员、兽医、医务工作者、派遣救济人员和其他人都有机会。 保健仍然是需求最有战略意义的领域之一。 全球卫生战略的IMB主任汤姆·希克斯(Tom Hicks)说,许多医疗专业人员对任务工作的看法是错误的. 他表示:「我们确实有个问题, 人们会选择出局, 事实上,Hicks说,全球许多地区正在越来越多地寻找家庭医学医生、实习医生、儿科医生、儿科护士、产科医生、物理治疗师、职业治疗师、语言病理学家和哺乳期咨询师。 这种需求在撒哈拉以南非洲尤为重要,那里的青年人口对儿科护理的需求日益增加。 在限制传教活动的国家,保健专业人员也提供了独特的优势。 「有职业价值的使团, 另一个经常被忽略的部是成员护理,重点是IMB传教士的精神、情感、心理和关系健康。 克里斯·马丁是IMB全球会员关怀的总监. Martin说,“会员关心传教士与那些传统上被认为是教会植树人或福音传教士的传教士站在一起并支持他们。” 担任这些角色的许多人来自咨询背景,帮助传教士应对压力、冲突、悲痛和其他挑战,这些挑战可能影响部委的长期效力。 马丁将他们的角色比作出埃及19号的Aaron和Hur,在战斗中举起摩西的手臂,强化了在前线服役的人. Sophia, an International Mission Board missionary, joined another IMB missionary and Maryam, a South Asian Christian. They went to the park to share the gospel, but approaching a man in their Muslim-majority city was out of the question. They kept walking and watching. Even if they went home without a single conversation, Sophia knew Maryam would want to try again. This woman who had grown up with a distrust of Muslims, now searched a park for a Muslim woman to tell about Jesus. When Sophia first invited her along, Maryam never imagined a Muslim could come to know Jesus. But the more they went out sharing the gospel together, the more God softened her heart. “One day, I found she was sharing in the park by herself, without me,” Sophia said with a laugh. These days, she shares regularly — with classmates, with rickshaw drivers, with women in the park, when she can find them. God transformed Maryam’s heart. He could transform this walk through the park, too. “So we stopped,” Sophia said, “and prayed, ‘God, give us just one woman to talk to.’” Then they spotted her — a girl sitting alone on a bench. Meeting the girl on the bench She looked like other conservative Muslim women in the area, covered in black except for her face. They approached casually, not wanting to frighten her. It was Eid al-Adha – “one of the biggest Muslim holidays here,” Sophia said. They greeted her and asked about her holiday plans. Her name was Tara, and she wasn’t intimidated at all. “You may think I’m a Muslim from the way I dress,” she said, “but actually in my heart, I have left Islam.” “I was a little shocked,” Sophia said, hearing such a bold statement from a stranger. Tara told them she was a university student at a conservative Islamic school, but she had grown disillusioned and discontent with the religion. “ I don’t believe in Islam anymore,” Tara said. Without knowledge of God, she had no one to pray to, and it left her lonely. She’d been searching — Buddhism and Hinduism from friends, even a meeting with atheists, who struck her as unhappy, following only themselves. “Do you know any Christians?” Sophia asked. “Would you like to hear what we believe?” “Sure, please share.” They read about Jesus’ birth, and Tara was hungry for more. When she asked about church, Sophia described their congregation of about 40 believers, many from a Muslim background. Though she wasn’t ready to visit the church, Tara continued her interest in learning. Sophia and Maryam met with her every week in coffee shops, tea shops, Sophia’s home, wherever they could talkthat wasn’t too loud or have “too many ears and eyes” observing them. Finding her closest friend They read through the Gospel of John. One November day in a coffee shop, they reached the passage on the Samaritan woman at the well, and Sophia noticed Tara was crying. “Tara, I see you have tears,” Sophia said. “Let’s stop. Let’s talk about it .” That day, Tara prayed to receive Christ. Soon after, she wanted to visit the church, though nervous how believers would receive her in a hijab. “They will love you,” Sophia told her. “Don’t worry.” Tara went and was welcomed. That Christmas, 80 people packed Sophia’s apartment, singing and dancing in circles. Across the room, Sophia saw Tara, wearing red Christmas garland like a scarf and a smile stretched across her face. “Tara grew up very conservative – music was not even allowed in her home. But now she’s dancing, worshiping the Lord with us with music and songs.” In South Asia, Maryam and a local pastor baptize Tara, a new believer. IMB missionaries work alongside local believers and churches to fulfill the Great Commission. IMB Photo That spring, Tara was baptized.

title_zh: 神通过IMB在意大利的传教士保持忠诚
content: The eastern face of St. Peter's Basilica in the Vatican City in Rome, Italy, is famous for its central balcony from which popes give their papal addresses. Most people in Rome have at least a cultural connection to Roman Catholicism as the city is “the heart of Catholicism.” IMB Photo In the city where Jason and Lizzy Davis serve, some steps have a lot of meaning. And the meaning is different for them than it is for the thousands who travel there to visit that site. “If you come to Rome, you can come to a place called the Holy Steps,” Jason said. “People go there, and they’ll crawl up on their knees and pray the rosary all the way up.” From the top of the steps, a mural depicting Jesus on the Cross looks down on those making the pilgrimage. For Jason and Lizzy, it’s a spiritual experience, a picture of a religion that asks people to earn their way to Jesus. “That’s really the opposite of what the gospel is. The gospel is Jesus saying, ‘No, you can’t do it . . . no matter how good you think you are,’” they said. Most people in Rome have at the very least a cultural connection to Roman Catholicism, as the city is “the heart of Catholicism.” Jason explained, “It’s where the Pope lives in the Vatican. It’s very much part of the religion and culture. It’s all intertwined here.” An ‘unavoidable’ call Jason and Lizzy are investing their lives as International Mission Board missionaries in Rome, Italy, to share the truth of the gospel. The Davises partner with national believers through a new church plant, and they’re seeking to plant more churches within the city. Lizzy said for her, the call to missions was unavoidable. “I grew up as a third culture kid, or a missionary kid. My parents were on the mission field, as were my grandparents, all with the International Mission Board.” Then her family moved to Virginia for her dad to work for IMB’s home office staff. As a middle schooler and high schooler, every time Lizzy heard about the need for the gospel to go forth, she felt a burden, a “burning” in her heart. She didn’t know what God would do with that, but she had a feeling she would see one day. Now, years later, she and Jason spend their time trying to find as many opportunities as they can to invite people into their home so they can share the hope of Jesus with them. That can mean Bible study or simply sharing a meal. ‘Completely lost’ Jason has been surprised by just how often people are willing to talk about faith. “You can get into spiritual conversations very quickly with people, especially if you’re just open and honest with them.” Lizzy shared that one of the easiest ways to do this is to be willing to let your day be interrupted. “That’s something I’ve seen Jason do firsthand in our neighborhood. He walks down the street, and everybody knows him because he stops and takes the time to ask them questions about their families, gets to know people, gets to know the newspaper stand guy and the guy at the fruit stand and the grocery store ladies.” She emphasized that caring about people is “what Christ would do.” The Davises, whose previous mission service prevents their photos from being published, live in a neighborhood of about 130,000 people. Their church of 15 people is the only evangelical congregation there. Lizzy said the area is “truly a lost, completely lost, dark neighborhood” with people who have never heard the gospel. Thousands more come to their area on a religious quest. The Davis family’s neighborhood is home to the Basilica Papale di San Paolo (the Papal Basilica of Saint Paul), one of the city’s four major basilicas. “So we get a lot of people coming on spiritual journeys, visiting our neighborhood, seeking some sort of spiritual experience. And oftentimes it’s just trying to earn their salvation,” she added. Jason described this environment as “a genuine need for people to actually hear the gospel and know that their sins can be forgiven and they can have an assurance of that.” IMB missionaries Jason and Liz

title_zh: 全球传教士合作伙伴通过IMB团队扩展福音工作
content: Rebeca Couto, a global missionary partner from the Azores islands, practices writing characters with her tutor in Japan. IMB Photo Rebeca Couto poses with her violin. Couto is a professional violinist who is serving as a global missionary partner with the IMB in Japan. Doors have opened for her to use her skills with evangel ical Japanese musicians who perform. IMB Photo Rebeca Couto moved from one volcanic archipelago to another, leaving Portugal’s Azores islands to anchor her life in Japan. The percentage of evangelical Christians in the Azores and Japan is similar, with both populations under 1%. Couto is a fourth-generation Christian, a rarity on the small islands. She is one of few, if any, believers in the Azores with such a long spiritual lineage. This rich legacy shaped her and prepared her for ministry. “I’ve always understood the Great Commission as a call for all believers and all disciples of Christ to be missionaries, wherever they are, whatever they’re doing, and whatever God has equipped them with,” Couto said. Couto’s great-grandfather became a Christian through the witness of missionaries from the United Kingdom. Later, missionaries from the Foreign Mission Board, now the International Mission Board, started the first Baptist work in the Azores by planting an English-speaking church near an American military base. A Baptist Brazilian couple planted a Portuguese-speaking church, which became the congregation where Couto grew up and was commissioned as a missionary. Ministry has been passed down through the generations of her family. Couto’s father has pastored for 20 years, and both of her parents have been involved in ministry for most of their lives. Couto now serves in Japan as a global missionary partner, a missionary who is financially supported by a sending church or organization in their home country and serves with IMB teams. Close to 400 GMPs currently serve on IMB teams around the world. Language learning Couto is immersed in language study in Yokohama, Japan. She had a head start before she even arrived. After graduating from high school, Couto moved from the Azores to Lisbon to pursue a degree in music. She spent hours on public transportation and wanted a challenge to pass the time. She decided to study Japanese because she thought it sounded beautiful. At the time, she had no intention of becoming a missionary in the traditional sense. However, the more she learned about the language and the culture, her burden for the lost grew. She began researching Christianity in Japan. “I understood how bleak the scenario was, and how much the country needed Jesus. I struggled with that calling because the doors were closed, and it didn’t seem possible to come to Japan for a myriad of reasons,” Couto said. After finishing master’s degrees in music and violin performance, along with a seminary degree, Couto was considering pursuing a Ph.D. or returning to seminary when her seminary professors, IMB missionaries Jonathan and Bethany Sharp, contacted her about serving as a missionary in Japan. They introduced her to the GMP program and invited her to attend a missions immersion school they piloted . Music to their ears As a professional violinist, Couto brought her violin to Japan, unsure of what opportunities existed, but she knew her call to the mission field somehow involved her gifting. “I see myself as having been called to serve through music. I never even conceived doing missions while excluding the violin entirely,” Couto said. She continued, “Music is such a universal way to connect with people, and it’s so intuitive to pair that with the gospel and with God’s message to people’s hearts.” While she knew the Lord would somehow open a door for her to use the violin for kingdom work, she was at peace with the possibility that, for a season, she may not be as active in music. title: IMB missionaries use home, cafes, apps to open doors for gospel conversations in Spain

title_zh: IMB传教士使用家庭、咖啡馆、应用程序为西班牙的福音对话敞开大门
content: Men and women gather to discuss spiritual topics with Caleb and Carina Beaty, International Mission Board missionaries who serve in Madrid. IMB Photo Across Spain, people looking for connection and meaningful conversation turn to the internet to find groups where they can meet others. At a café by the river, Caleb and Carina Beaty engage in conversations about finding purpose, beauty and “what’s wrong with the world.” A website called Meetup allows people to search for groups to meet in person. The description of the Beatys’ group indicates that it discusses spiritual topics. People come expecting to talk about faith, so it’s not a surprise when they arrive. Caleb said he always has a list of questions that begin broadly and funnel into questions such as, “If there were a God …” or “What do you think Christians believe about that?” or “Why do you think religions have such different perspectives?” The Beatys’ goal in these conversations is to work toward deeper worldview questions within 45 minutes to an hour. Most of the people who attend their Meetup group are from Madrid, but they also have conversations with people from other countries. During one Meetup, Caleb and Carina shared how creation was perfect, but sin led to a world separated from the Father. God offers salvation through the death and resurrection of Jesus, they explained. “There are times we’re able to get to a clear gospel presentation with a group of people, and sometimes we’re doing pre-evangelism.” Caleb said. Some repeat attendees who have been attending for more than a year quickly jump to the heart of the discussion. “All right, Caleb, what’s the Bible say about suffering?” they’ll ask. Caleb and Carina then have the opportunity to share the Christian perspective. IMB missionaries Caleb and Carina Beaty and their children pose for a photo in a park in Madrid, Spain.  IMB Photo Spain has secularized rapidly since the 1990s, Caleb said. While many may think of it as a Catholic nation, many people do not know the basic tenets of Christianity. “We’ve got all the churches, we’ve got the cathedrals, and they do processions, but the average person on the street does not know anything about the gospel and does not know anything about Jesus,” Caleb said. Younger Spaniards are drawn to their group and are receptive to the gospel because they don’t have a spiritual foundation or know anyone who does. “There’s just this curiosity because, for a lot of them, they’ve never met someone who actually believes that God exists, and that changes your life,” Carina said. “I’ve had people completely shocked that we believe in God. ‘You really believe that God exists?’ They can’t wrap their mind around that.” During one Meetup, a man contrasted Protestant and Catholic beliefs by saying Protestants focus on Jesus’ suffering and Catholics on Mary’s grief. Caleb responded that evangelicals focus on the resurrection. When Caleb said Jesus rose from the dead, the man replied that he needed to look into that. Caleb said encounters like that reveal how little many Spaniards know about the gospel. Caleb noted the irony of the man’s sharing the Catholic perspective without truly understanding it. He is not the only person the Beatys have met who has missed the heart of the gospel. A friend of the Beatys told them she’d heard Jesus died, but she hadn’t heard he rose from the dead. A man reads a passage of Scripture during a Bible study hosted by IMB missionaries Caleb and Carina Beaty at their family’s apartment in Madrid, Spain. Five atheists began attending their Bible study after attending the couple’s Meetup group. IMB Photo The Beatys also host seasonal outreach events through the Meetup. Members from their church in Madrid have started attending the Meetup to learn how the Beatys lead discussions. Their group has become so popular, a waitlist has formed. Caleb and Carina host a small-group Bible study in their home. Five atheists who joined their Meetup now attend the Bible study.

The Lottie Moon Christmas Offering® (LMCO) totaled $212.5 million to support International Mission Board (IMB) missionaries, and the Annie Armstrong Easter Offering® (AAEO) reached $73.6 million to support the North American Mission Board’s (NAMB) church planting, compassion ministry and other evangelistic efforts to reach North America. With giving through the Lottie Moon offering at an all-time high, churches and individual givers continue to display a heart for the gospel to be proclaimed to every nation, all tribes, peoples and languages,” Chitwood said. The Annie total marked the second highest in NAMB’s history. The record Lottie Moon offering total surpassed last year’s total by more than $5 million and is the best offering in IMB history. “God is giving our generation unprecedented opportunity to send missionaries to the most unreached peoples and places,” Chitwood continued. “Though the challenges faced by our missionaries are enormous, the generosity of Southern Baptists ensures they have what they need to face those challenges and continue in the work while we hold the ropes with our support.” IMB missionary Landon Williams (center) walks with a Chilean pastor and a U.S. pastor on a remote island in Chile. Cooperation and generosity among Southern Baptists fuels the work to reach the uttermost parts of the world with the gospel. IMB Photo National goals for both offerings are set in partnership with Woman’s Missionary Union (WMU) each year. In response to the offering totals, Sandy Wisdom-Martin, executive director-treasurer of WMU, said: “As Southern Baptists, we are all in for His mission. When we give sacrificially, we prioritize the mission of God. Together our fervent prayers, our faithful generosity and our wholehearted obedience become channels for the gospel to reach our neighbors as well as the nations.” For the last 10 years, Southern Baptists have increasingly supported the Annie offering, setting records in seven of the last 10 years. Totals in each of the last four years have surpassed $70 million. “I am so grateful to the pastors and churches for the faithfulness and generosity they have demonstrated through this offering,” said NAMB president Kevin Ezell. “As I travel and speak in churches of all sizes, I love seeing the posters in the hallways showing their offering goals. In 2025, Southern Baptists planted the largest number of churches, 699, since 2016. Including church plants and replants, Southern Baptists have surpassed 700 new churches in four of the last five years. More than 12,000 churches have been planted since 2010. title_zh: 俄克拉荷马州浸信会加入派遣教会实验室，以加强传教士支持
content: Staff members at First Baptist Church in Wagoner, Oklahoma, evaluate their church’s involvement with missions and missionary support. IMB Photo The chapel at Council Road Baptist Church in Oklahoma City turned into a science lab on Oct. 5-6. Microscopes, beakers and test tubes weren’t in the room, but this Sending Church Lab drew nearly 40 people representing 12 Oklahoma Baptist churches committed to send and care for international missionaries well. The Sending Church Lab, facilitated by the International Mission Board, brought pastors, church leaders and missionaries together for two days of discussion, self-assessment and planning centered on one question: What does it mean for a church to truly be a sending church? For Mike Wall, a global missions ministry partner of Oklahoma Baptists, the answer begins with churches reclaiming responsibility for the Great Commission. Wall first attended a Sending Church Lab last year in Tulsa with few expectations. He left convinced more churches needed the training. “When I went there, I thought, ‘You’ve got to do this in Oklahoma City,’” Wall said, “because of the content and how much our churches need something just like this.” After observing churches work through the exercises in the lab, Wall said he was encouraged by an emphasis on local church ownership in missions. “We can’t just send our people and say, ‘OK, now this is your job, IMB,’” he said. “We have to do our job in sending, preparing and training the best ‘sent ones’ so that when they get to the field, they can already hit the ground running.” Bryan Wooten, IMB senior church engagement specialist, leads a Sending Church Lab at Council Road Baptist Church in Oklahoma City. He is emphasizing the importance of sending churches assessing and equipping future IMB missionaries. IMB Photo Leading the lab was Bryan Wooten, IMB senior church engagement strategist, who developed the concept after seeing the need for stronger relationships between missionaries and local churches. “A Sending Church Lab is our attempt to raise up a host of IMB sending churches,” Wooten said, crediting the North American Mission Board for doing similar events and having successful results. The lab helps churches understand what Wooten calls the church engagement pathway: praying, cooperating, partnering and sending. While many churches faithfully pray, give and go, he said sending requires something more intentional. “Sending includes taking responsibility for an IMB missionary by providing ongoing encouragement, accountability and soul care throughout their term of service,” he explained. During the two-day event, participants gathered around whiteboards to evaluate their church’s missions practices, identify strengths and weaknesses and develop plans for improvement. “We don’t just need to deliver content,” Wooten said. “We need to invite churches to do some work on their own.” Rather than simply listening to presentations, attendees worked through practical questions about prayer, giving, short-term missions, missionary assessment and long-term care. Wooten said churches consistently tell him the greatest benefit is clarity. “They are thankful for clarity on what an IMB sending church is and what our roles and responsibilities are,” he said. For IMB missionaries Peter and Katie Weeks, that clarity is especially valuable. They participated in the lab alongside church leaders. Their real names have been changed to protect their work in Southeast Asia. “There’s no other place I’d rather be during these few days than here,” Peter said. Katie appreciated the interactive nature of the training. “I really appreciate the way they’re actually requiring information from the different churches and encouraging dialogue about how they can go through the steps,” she said. From a missionary perspective, she believes the lab addresses a common challenge. “It’s hard to know sometimes as churches how to be a good sending church and how to support missionaries,” she sa
content_zh: 俄克拉何马州瓦戈纳第一浸信会的工作人员评价了教会参与传教和传教活动的情况。 IMB 相片 俄克拉荷马城Constitute Road Baptist Church的小教堂于10月5-6日变成科学实验室. 但这个送信教会实验室吸引了近40人, 代表12个俄克拉何马浸会教会, 传教士实验室在国际传教委员会的协助下,召集牧师、教会领袖和传教士进行两天的讨论、自我评估和规划,其中心是一个问题: 教会真正成为送教之所意味着什么? 对于俄克拉何马浸信会的全球使命部合作伙伴迈克·沃尔来说,答案始于教会重新为大委员会负责。 去年沃尔在图尔萨参加了一个送教实验室, 他离开后确信更多的教会需要训练. “当我去那里时,我想,`你必须在俄克拉荷马城做这件事,'墙说,`因为内容和我们的教会需要这样的东西。 在观察了教堂通过实验室的演练工作后,沃尔说,他在任务中强调当地教会的所有权使他受到鼓舞. “我们不能只是派我们的人来说,“好吧,这是你的工作,IMB。” “我们必须在派遣、准备和训练最优秀的`派遣 ' 人员方面完成我们的工作,这样,当他们到达实地时,他们就已经可以奔跑地了。” Bryan Wooten,IMB高级教会订婚专家,在俄克拉荷马城的Constitution Road Baptist教堂领导一个送教实验室. 他强调派遣教会评估和装备未来的IMB传教士的重要性. IMB Photo Leading the lab是IMB高级教会接触策略师布莱恩·伍滕(Bryan Wooten),他在看到传教士与本地教会之间需要更牢固的关系后发展出这个概念. 伍腾说,“一个派遣教会实验室是我们努力培养许多派遣教会的IMB。 ”他赞扬北美传教委员会开展了类似的活动并取得了成功。 实验室帮助教会理解伍腾所谓的教会参与途径:祈祷,合作,合作和发送. 虽然许多教堂忠实地祈祷,奉献和去,但他说送去需要更有意图的东西. 他解释说,“最后包括负责一个IMB传教士,在整个任职期间提供持续的鼓励、问责和精神关怀。” 在为期两天的活动期间,与会者聚集在白板周围,评价其教会的任务做法,查明优缺点并制订改进计划。 」伍腾说: “我们需要邀请教会自己做一些工作。” 与会者不是简单地听取演讲,而是通过祷告、赠送、短期访问、传教士评估和长期照料等实际问题开展工作。 Wooten说,教会总是告诉他最大的好处是清晰. 他说,“他们感谢对派遣教会的咨监委的澄清,以及我们的作用和责任。” 对于IMB的传教士彼得和凯蒂·威克斯来说,这种清晰度特别有价值. 他们与教会领袖一起参加了实验室. 他们的真名被更改以保护自己在东南亚的工作. 彼得说,“在这几天里,我宁愿呆在这里。” 凯蒂对培训的互动性表示赞赏. 我非常欣赏他们要求不同教会提供信息的方式, 从传教士的角度来看,她认为实验室解决了共同的挑战. title_zh: 数字化之门为东南亚岛民打开福音之门
content: Just as young people today have become more comfortable with talking online than in person, the same is true for people in Southeast Asia. IMB missionaries are creating and publishing Jesus-focused ads, videos and other digital content to connect with the lost through the internet. IMB Photo Recently, an International Mission Board team in Southeast Asia asked a young woman if she had heard the story of Jesus. She replied that, yes, she had heard about Him through a video online! “Back in the day,” shared Amanda Clarkston, an IMB missionary who has served in Southeast Asia for 33 years, “when I first came on the field, you’d go somewhere and gather all the people together in the village to watch the JESUS film.” Now, face-to-face conversations about Christ on the Southeast Asian islands are harder to accomplish. While teams travel to these remote islands often, living in a sparsely populated, animistic background culture as a foreigner creates suspicion and make long-term ministry difficult. Furthermore, young people today have become more comfortable with talking online than they are in person, Clarkston said, which is true of the islanders as well. Attempting to have a spiritual conversation face-to-face has become “too much” for locals, Clarkston shared. So, how do you share the gospel with multiple people groups who are constantly online and less comfortable with in-person interactions? For these Southeast Asia teams, digital engagement — the use of social media platforms to share a message — has become a plausible and effective entry point. The social media agency We Are Social confirmed this, revealing that 82.4% of Southeast Asia’s population uses the internet. “No matter where they go, how far they go, how remote it is, people have phones,” Clarkston and her team realized, “And though sometimes they do have to climb up the highest peak to get reception, people do it.” Clarkston’s team has begun creating and publishing Jesus-focused ads, videos and other digital content in hopes of building bridges to the islanders through the internet. Viewers can click on the ad to message back and forth with a responder, a local believer or missionary who is available to pray, build relationships and answer spiritual questions. “It seems like locals are more open to watching those things in the privacy of their own cell phones,” Clarkston said. Clarkston intends to use digital engagement as a means for initial contact with people with animistic backgrounds, evangelism and, eventually, discipleship. She said that this new ministry has the potential to open doors with individuals across these islands who would normally never reach out on their own or respond to the gospel in person. “Maybe they’ll respond this way,” Clarkston said, “I know without a shadow of a doubt that God is calling people to Himself.” Now, more than ever, technology has a grip on society. Many spend hours each day mindlessly scrolling, searching for meaning, for happiness. And now, more than ever, there is an incredible opportunity to plant seeds across Southeast Asian islands through digital engagement. The IMB Southeast Asia team gives praise to the Lord that He has provided a creative way to reach the lost and plant seeds. Pray the people among the Southeast Asian islands would see these ads and engage with responders boldly, even though they may face persecution or harm because of it. Names were changed for security. Mikah Young is serving overseas with the IMB. The work of the IMB is sustained through faithful giving to the Cooperative Program and the Lottie Moon Christmas Offering ® .
