title_zh: IMB传教士在服务之旅中分享首尔的愿景
content: Ask most people what comes to mind when they think of South Korea, and they’ll likely mention K-pop, skincare, cutting-edge technology, or bustling city streets filled with young professionals. Hun and Eunjoo Sol see those things too. But after more than a decade serving as International Mission Board missionaries in Seoul, they also see something many visitors never notice. “Many people think that Korea is exciting and successful,” Hun said. “They think about the K-pop, the K-culture, K-technology, K-cosmetics. Yes, good things… But many Korean people are struggling right now.” The Sols, who were featured in the 2025 Week of Prayer for International Missions , continue to rely on the prayers of faithful Southern Baptists. Prayers sustain them and help to push back the darkness they confront in their home culture. Hun often describes that hidden struggle with a Korean word: han. There is no simple English translation. It speaks to a deep sorrow shaped by generations of war, division, loss, and the quiet resolve to endure. Hun sees it in the young adults he meets every week—people navigating loneliness and relentless expectations, quietly asking what their lives are for beneath a veneer of success. Han is heavy. For many young adults, that weight can feel unbearable. Suicide is one of the leading causes of death among teenagers and young adults in South Korean. Hun and Eunjoo see the effects of that reality every day, and it’s one reason they believe they have no time to waste. That understanding shaped the week of Serve Tour Seoul this summer. There were no construction sites, no paintbrushes, no tools or work gloves. Instead, the team stepped into ministries local churches had been faithfully building long before the volunteers arrived. In May, 27 volunteers from seven churches across the United States came alongside local churches already serving their communities in Seoul, Paju, and Gwangju. They taught English classes, ran children’s camps, walked neighborhoods in prayer, distributed food, and sat down with college students, one conversation at a time. For Nick Holst of Sandals Church in Riverside, California, the goal was simple enough to say in a sentence: “We came to meet people,” Holst said. “We want to hear their stories, and that leads to some very meaningful connections as you get past the surface into something deeper.” That’s where the week actually lived: past the surface and past the small talk, where the quiet weight of han is often carried without words. On college campuses, volunteers played games, asked questions and mostly just listened. Some conversations lasted a few minutes and ended there. Others kept going long past the point where either person expected them to. One morning, after asking his church back home to pray, Holst sat down with a university student named Intec. They talked about culture first, the way strangers do, and then the conversation turned somewhere neither of them planned. “I got to ask him, ‘What do Koreans believe?’” Holst recalled. Intec said he didn’t believe in God. Then he recited John 3:16 from memory, word for word, a verse he’d heard somewhere along the way and never forgotten. Before they parted, Holst asked if he could pray that God would keep drawing Intec toward Himself. “He said yes.” In a city where many conversations never move beyond the surface, the exchange was a reminder of why the team had come. Not to win an argument, but to listen, to ask questions, and to trust God with what happens next. The same pattern unfolded elsewhere, beginning in classrooms and ending on city streets. Jeremy Doyle, missions pastor at Valley Baptist Church in Bakersfield, California, watched an English conversation club grow from two students on its first night to eight by the second. Nobody advertised it as anything more than a place to practice English, but the room kept filling, and so did the conversations. The team’s work with students didn’t stop there. content: What did your journey to faith look like? Perhaps it was a story of how God showed up in the midst of uncertainty, doubt or fears. Maybe it involved Him seeking you out and rescuing you. Or maybe you grew up in a Christian household and your story is a bit different — perhaps your family regularly read the Bible together and have always known about Jesus’ love. Ken Trager was raised that way. He reflected, “I think when you’re raised in a Christian home … and you have the routines of a life that is built around church and prayer, you just take it for granted.” He added, “It was just the air I breathed.” For Ken and his wife, Sally, faith was always part of their stories. They were each raised in Christian homes, followed Christ, got baptized and had parents who faithfully modeled church attendance, prayer and generosity.  Ken and Sally’s paths eventually crossed at Greenville University in southern Illinois, where they met and fell in love. They went on to build a life centered around family, faith and service. Ken spent his career as a teacher and coach while Sally worked as an accountant, and together they raised two children. Now retired, they’ve moved to be closer to their children and grandchildren, giving them a new opportunity to pour into the next generation. Through all those years and seasons, the faith Ken and Sally had seen modeled by their families continued to shape their home. Early in their marriage, Ken and Sally met a mentor who encouraged the couple to go deeper with their faith — to study Scripture, ask questions and wrestle honestly with what they believed. It was an important season of discovering that the faith that had been passed down from their families could also become something they personally owned and lived out together. What Do You Take for Granted? Years later, the couple experienced an aha moment when they were introduced to Wycliffe at an event. There, Ken and Sally heard story after story from people who had received Scripture in their own languages. Something clicked for Sally: “We’ve never known a day where we couldn’t access the Bible. And these people have just longed for it, and they’re finally getting it.” For the first time, something that had always surrounded the couple became visible — and it was a gift they could no longer take for granted . Ken and Sally had spent years thinking about the importance of God’s Word. Seeing people receive Scripture in their own languages helped them understand just how extraordinary that access is. “The power of salvation comes through that,” Ken said. “I can’t think of … [a more] important work than providing God’s Word to everybody in the world.” Sally agreed. “To have His Word is as if we’re hearing the voice of God,” she said. “God works through His Word.” This conviction — for people around the world to be able to access Scripture for themselves — became one of the reasons Ken and Sally prioritized a place in their giving for Wycliffe. But it also became part of a larger question about generosity they had been asking themselves for years: “If everything we have is a gift from God, what does it look like to live generously with it?” A Generous Heart Generosity, like faith, was something Ken and Sally had grown up around. Ken remembers his dad giving him money to put in the offering plate, and Sally remembers watching her parents give not just to their church but to people and organizations in need. Sally’s father especially enjoyed giving anonymously. As Ken and Sally have grown older, they’ve learned that generosity isn’t simply about giving a certain percentage or checking a box; it’s about continually asking what it means to have a generous heart . For Ken, the question of what it means to be generous has become what he calls “Kingdom Advancement Giving.” When contemplating giving, he asks, “Is this going to advance the Kingdom for God’s glory?” That question has shaped the way the couple thinks about which individuals and organizations they

你的信仰之旅是什么样子的? 也许这是上帝如何在不确定、怀疑或恐惧中出现的故事。 也许这涉及到他寻找你 并救你。 或者你在一个基督教家庭长大,你的故事有点不同——也许你的家人经常一起阅读圣经,并且一直知道耶稣的爱。 肯崔格是那样长大的

他回想道 , “ 我想当你在基督教家庭长大... 你有一个在教堂和祷告周围建造的日常生活, 你只是把它视为理所当然。 ” 他又说:“只是我呼吸的空气。” 对于肯和他的妻子莎莉来说,信仰总是他们的故事的一部分.

他们各自在基督教家中长大,跟随基督,接受洗礼,并有忠实的模范教会出席,祈祷和慷慨的父母. 肯和莎莉的道路最终在伊利诺伊州南部的格林维尔大学交叉,在那里他们相遇并坠入爱河. 他们继续建立一个以家庭、信仰和服务为中心的生活。

肯在萨利担任会计期间度过了教师和教练的生涯,两人一起抚养两个孩子. 他们已经退休了, 他们已经搬到更亲近他们的儿孙, 给他们一个新的机会, 注入下一代。 在那些年和季节中,肯和莎莉所见到的由家人塑造的信仰继续塑造自己的家园.

早年的婚姻中,肯和莎莉结识了一位导师,他鼓励这对夫妇更深入地信仰——学习圣经,提出问题,并诚实地与所相信的东西搏斗. 这是一个重要的季节,发现从家人传下来的信仰也可能成为他们个人拥有和共同生活的东西. 你拿什么给格兰特?

多年后,夫妇俩在一次活动上被介绍到怀克利夫(Wycliffe)时,经历了一段愉快的时刻. 在那里,肯和莎莉从以自己语言接受圣经的人那里听到一个接一个的故事. “我们从未知道有一天我们无法阅读圣经。

而这些人也只是渴望, 第一次,一直包围着这对夫妇的东西变得明显——这是他们不能再视为理所当然的礼物了. 肯和莎莉花了多年时间思考上帝之言的重要性.

看到人们用自己的语言接受圣经 有助于他们理解这种访问是多么非凡 肯说,“救赎的力量来自此”。 " 我无法想象......比向全世界每个人提供上帝的话更重要的工作。 " 萨莉同意了 ”她说,

“真主通过他的话而工作。” 这种信念——让世界各地的人们能够为自己获得圣经——成为肯和莎莉在为威克利夫奉献一个位置时优先考虑的原因之一.

但是,它也成为了一个更大的问题的一部分,即他们多年来一直问自己:“如果我们所拥有的一切是上帝的礼物,那么与它慷慨相处是什么样子?” 和信仰一样 善良的心是肯和莎莉成长的

肯记得父亲给了他钱放进祭品盘中,莎莉记得看着她的父母不仅把钱送给他们的教堂,还送给需要帮助的人和组织. Sally的父亲特别喜欢匿名赠送。 肯和莎莉已经长大了, 他们已经了解到慷慨不只是给予一定的百分比或检查一个盒子。

需要不断问, 对肯来说,慷慨意味着什么的问题已经变成了他所谓的“提高国王地位”的问题。 当他考虑施舍的时候,他问道:"这难道是为了真主的荣耀而推动王国吗? 这个问题决定了夫妻双方对哪些个人和组织的看法

content: How old were you when you first learned that Jesus loves you? Perhaps you’ve always known it and can’t remember a day when you didn’t know the song “Jesus Loves Me” or couldn’t recite John 3:16 by heart. Maybe you were a teenager and learned about Jesus’ love through a friend or church summer camp. Or were in college and went to a concert where the gospel was clearly articulated. Maybe you were in the trenches of the workforce, and a coworker boldly shared with you about the God who radically changed their life. Regardless of how old you were, each of us who has chosen to follow Jesus has an origin story — a moment in our lives when the knowledge that “Jesus loves me, this I know, for the Bible tells me so” moved from head knowledge to heart belief. And from then on, our lives were transformed forever. This is the truth of the gospel and the power of understanding that Jesus loves you. People around the world are discovering the personal truth of John 3:16 for themselves in a language and format they clearly understand. Explore why understanding that “God so loved the world” transforms entire communities → A Changing Reality Throughout Christian history, the gospel has spread from one community to the next. Stories were told and retold, Scripture was translated, churches were planted, and discipleship deepened as people learned more about Jesus. Bible translation is foundational to all ministries of the church. It fuels evangelism, church planting, discipleship and more. It equips people to move from a blurry picture of who God is to a clear understanding and personal encounter with Jesus as Lord. Through Scripture, people are able to read, hear or see the love of God on display. Just two decades ago, most of the world’s language communities still needed Bible translation work to begin , let alone be completed. But praise God, in the last few years, we’ve seen tremendous progress made, with Bible translation underway in more languages than ever before . While the change in numbers is exciting, what’s more important is what they signify: Every number represents a person who has a story that matters to God. For these communities, the stories of future generations are being completely rewritten as children will now grow up never remembering a day when they didn’t have access to God’s Word in a language and format they clearly understand. That statement bears repeating: There will now be people who never remember a day when they didn’t have access to God’s Word in a language and format they clearly understand. From the first word of Genesis to the last word of Revelation, the Bible tells one incredible story: God’s love for the world and His invitation for people from every nation and language to know Him. Get a glimpse of how God continues writing this story today as more and more people are experiencing the power of His Word. Watch the video → A New Generation Growing Up With God’s Word Let’s take a look at some of the recent communities that are experiencing not only life transformation but generational transformation as they encounter Jesus personally through Scripture. Jakalteko | Guatemala The Jakalteko Bible was dedicated in July 2026 in Guatemala! During the celebration, John 1:1-18 was read aloud — a passage that focuses on Christ, the eternal Word and our Redeemer. Early on, many women in the community memorized Job 19 . Like Job, they had faced various hardships in their lives and identified with his suffering. The book reminded them that God remains in control and that, in the midst of difficult circumstances, their Redeemer will deliver them and comfort them in their pain. Today, they have the full counsel of God’s Word and can now see this Redeemer fulfilled in Jesus in the New Testament. They are overjoyed that the Bible has arrived in the language they were born into! When the Bible was distributed, one mother who is raising her family alone said with joy and tears: “Thank God we have the Bible in our language. Now

title: Finding Wonder in the Midst of Christmas Weariness
source: Wycliffe Bible Translators · 译经故事
summary: Rediscover the wonder of Christmas by focusing on God’s faithfulness and the hope found in Jesus.   The post  Finding Wonder in the Midst of Christmas Weariness  appeared first on  Wycliffe .
summary_zh: 通过关注神的信实和耶稣的盼望，重新发现圣诞节的奇迹。“在圣诞节疲惫中寻找奇迹”一文首次出现在威克里夫。
title_zh: 在圣诞节疲惫中寻找奇迹
content: Christmas is supposed to be a season of wonder. Twinkling lights, familiar songs, meaningful traditions and time with people you love can all point toward the joy of celebrating Jesus’ birth. But when your December calendar fills with responsibilities and expectations, weariness can settle in before you realize it. Maybe you remember a time when Christmas felt different. As a child, you may have counted down the days and experienced joy in even the smallest traditions. As an adult, you might find yourself simply trying to catch your breath as you move from one responsibility to the next. In the middle of trying to make Christmas special for everyone else, it can be easy to miss the wonder yourself. But the Christmas story gives you an opportunity to slow down and remember what this season is really about. In Luke 1, before the story of Jesus’ birth begins, you meet people who knew what it meant to wait, wonder and trust that God was at work even when they couldn’t yet see what He was doing. Weary of Waiting Luke’s account of the life of Jesus doesn’t begin with Jesus’ birth; it begins instead with the story of Zechariah, an elderly priest who was tired of waiting. Zechariah had heard promises of Israel’s rescue from oppression and sin his entire life. That future must have seemed out of reach under Rome’s harsh control. But Zechariah and his wife, Elizabeth, also had an unfulfilled personal longing: “They had no children because Elizabeth was unable to conceive, and they were both very old” ( Luke 1:7, NLT ). One day, as Zechariah performed his duties in the temple, he was chosen to burn incense in the sanctuary — a rare honor with an unexpected result: While Zechariah was in the sanctuary, an angel of the Lord appeared to him, standing to the right of the incense altar. Zechariah was shaken and overwhelmed with fear when he saw him. But the angel said, “Don’t be afraid, Zechariah! God has heard your prayer. Your wife, Elizabeth, will give you a son, and you are to name him John. You will have great joy and gladness, and many will rejoice at his birth, for he will be great in the eyes of the Lord. He must never touch wine or other alcoholic drinks. He will be filled with the Holy Spirit, even before his birth. And he will turn many Israelites to the Lord their God. He will be a man with the spirit and power of Elijah. He will prepare the people for the coming of the Lord. He will turn the hearts of the fathers to their children, and he will cause those who are rebellious to accept the wisdom of the godly” ( Luke 1:11-17, NLT ). Trusting God in the Waiting An angel of the Lord appeared to Zechariah and announced that God had heard his prayer. Elizabeth would have a son named John who would “… prepare the people for the coming of the Lord” ( Luke 1:17b, NLT ). After years of waiting, God answered Zechariah and Elizabeth’s prayer as part of an even bigger story: They would finally have the child they had prayed for, and their son would prepare the way for Jesus. But Zechariah struggled to understand how it could possibly happen: “… ‘How can I be sure this will happen? I’m an old man now, and my wife is also well along in years’” ( Luke 1:18, NLT ). Zechariah could only see what seemed possible based on his circumstances. But God was asking him to trust what He had promised. The angel Gabriel responded by telling Zechariah that he would be unable to speak until the child was born, adding, “For my words will certainly be fulfilled at the proper time” ( Luke 1:20b, NLT ). Maybe you know what it’s like to pray about something for months or even years. It can be hard to keep trusting that God is working when it seems like nothing is changing. Zechariah’s story reminds us that even when we can’t see what God is doing, He is still faithful to His promises. Waiting is woven throughout the Christmas story. Maybe it’s part of your story too. content: Imagine reading a book, watching a show or listening to a podcast when suddenly the story just stops mid-sentence. Maybe the previous reader has ripped out a page, the series was canceled before the showrunners could wrap up the plotline, or the producer distributed the episode before realizing it was incomplete. How incredibly frustrating to not experience the full story from start to finish! It can leave us emotionally unsettled, frustrated or even distraught, because at our core, we desire completion. We want to know how things start and how they end. We don’t just want a taste, because it feels like a tease. We’re left wanting more . And we’re not alone in that desire! The same is true for communities around the world who are still waiting for the full counsel of God’s Word in a language and format they clearly understand. For some, they’re still waiting for the first verse of Scripture to be translated into their language. Others might have a few verses, chapters or Scripture portions . Still others are blessed with a complete New Testament but are waiting for the Old Testament so they can understand everything from Genesis to Revelation. They get a teaser of God’s great story — perhaps enough to understand who Jesus is and that He died for them — but they don’t have the full context as to why His sacrifice was so significant. The Bible changes everything, and together with our partners, Wycliffe believes that everyone should have access to the whole of Scripture. But don’t just take our word for it! Explore these Bible translation stories from our friends around the world who have personally experienced individual and community transformation as a result of encountering God through His Word. Want a glimpse of what it’s like to only have a portion of God’s Word? This “H ly B bl: Incomplete Scriptures” digital booklet helps you see what it’s like to have gaps in your understanding of the Bible. Explore the booklet → The Full “Outfit” of God’s Word Caroline always had access to a Bible growing up. But watching the Chonyi people of Kenya receive the New Testament in their language refreshed her passion for Bible translation, a mission she’s actively engaged in through SIL Kenya, a partner of Wycliffe. “They took a couple of Bibles, wrapped them up like a child,” she shared. “And there was a woman who was carrying the [Bibles]. And they were swinging and dancing, lifting up the [Bibles] and saying, ‘This is our child.’ Calling people, ‘Come,” in the Chonyi language. ‘Come and celebrate the child that has been born in us.’ “That is how the Chonyi people have taken the Bible — the New Testament — in their own language. That it is their child and they’re taking it seriously, making it bear fruit.” People gathered to hear Scripture read in their language, Bible studies began and the impact spread: 300 adults and 50 children gave their lives to Christ! At the celebration, the local pastors shared that now that the New Testament is complete, it’s like they have a shirt. But a shirt isn’t enough; they want a pair of pants (the Old Testament) to complete the outfit! Now work is underway to translate the Old Testament into Chonyi so that they can have the full “outfit” of God’s Word. Praise God! Watch how the Chonyi community celebrated the dedication of the New Testament in their community! As her neighbors listened alongside her, they became captivated by the story of Jesus. One day, someone from the community called the local translation office with a request. “We have been enjoying this Jesus story from this elderly woman, and now it has broken. summary: Today on the Faithly Podcast, Alicia Lee welcomes Melissa Paredes, Senior Director of Content Marketing at Wycliffe Bible Translators USA, for a meaningful conversation about Bible translation, motherhood, and the life-changing power of Scripture.   The post  When God’s Word Becomes Personal  appeared first on  Wycliffe .
summary_zh: 今天，在Faithly播客上， Alicia Lee欢迎Wycliffe Bible Translators USA内容营销高级总监Melissa Paredes就圣经翻译、母性以及圣经改变生活的力量进行有意义的对话。当上帝的话语成为个人时，这篇文章首先出现在威克里夫。
title_zh: 当神的话变成个人的
content: How old were you when you first learned that Jesus loves you? Perhaps you’ve always known it and can’t remember a day when you didn’t know the song “Jesus Loves Me” or couldn’t recite John 3:16 by heart. Maybe you were a teenager and learned about Jesus’ love through a friend or church summer camp. Or were in college and went to a concert where the gospel was clearly articulated. Maybe you were in the trenches of the workforce, and a coworker boldly shared with you about the God who radically changed their life. Regardless of how old you were, each of us who has chosen to follow Jesus has an origin story — a moment in our lives when the knowledge that “Jesus loves me, this I know, for the Bible tells me so” moved from head knowledge to heart belief. And from then on, our lives were transformed forever. This is the truth of the gospel and the power of understanding that Jesus loves you. People around the world are discovering the personal truth of John 3:16 for themselves in a language and format they clearly understand. Explore why understanding that “God so loved the world” transforms entire communities → A Changing Reality Throughout Christian history, the gospel has spread from one community to the next. Stories were told and retold, Scripture was translated, churches were planted, and discipleship deepened as people learned more about Jesus. Bible translation is foundational to all ministries of the church. It fuels evangelism, church planting, discipleship and more. It equips people to move from a blurry picture of who God is to a clear understanding and personal encounter with Jesus as Lord. Through Scripture, people are able to read, hear or see the love of God on display. Just two decades ago, most of the world’s language communities still needed Bible translation work to begin , let alone be completed. But praise God, in the last few years, we’ve seen tremendous progress made, with Bible translation underway in more languages than ever before . While the change in numbers is exciting, what’s more important is what they signify: Every number represents a person who has a story that matters to God. For these communities, the stories of future generations are being completely rewritten as children will now grow up never remembering a day when they didn’t have access to God’s Word in a language and format they clearly understand. That statement bears repeating: There will now be people who never remember a day when they didn’t have access to God’s Word in a language and format they clearly understand. From the first word of Genesis to the last word of Revelation, the Bible tells one incredible story: God’s love for the world and His invitation for people from every nation and language to know Him. Get a glimpse of how God continues writing this story today as more and more people are experiencing the power of His Word. Watch the video → A New Generation Growing Up With God’s Word Let’s take a look at some of the recent communities that are experiencing not only life transformation but generational transformation as they encounter Jesus personally through Scripture. Jakalteko | Guatemala The Jakalteko Bible was dedicated in July 2026 in Guatemala! During the celebration, John 1:1-18 was read aloud — a passage that focuses on Christ, the eternal Word and our Redeemer. Early on, many women in the community memorized Job 19 . Like Job, they had faced various hardships in their lives and identified with his suffering. The book reminded them that God remains in control and that, in the midst of difficult circumstances, their Redeemer will deliver them and comfort them in their pain. Today, they have the full counsel of God’s Word and can now see this Redeemer fulfilled in Jesus in the New Testament. They are overjoyed that the Bible has arrived in the language they were born into! When the Bible was distributed, one mother who is raising her family alone said with joy and tears: “Thank God we have the Bible in our language. Now

title: When Generosity Becomes Worship
source: Wycliffe Bible Translators · 译经故事
summary: Discover how Millie anchored herself in God’s Word during difficult circumstances — and how that shapes her view of generosity.   The post  When Generosity Becomes Worship  appeared first on  Wycliffe .
summary_zh: 了解Millie在困难情况下如何在神的话语中扎根，以及这如何塑造她对慷慨的看法。《When Generosity Becomes Worship》一文首次出现在《Wycliffe》上。
title_zh: 当慷慨成为崇拜
content: What circumstances or experiences have shaped your life? For 93-year-old Millie (name changed), her testimony was shaped by the Great Depression and deep loss, but also by an enduring faith and a lifetime of seeing God’s faithfulness unfold. Every chapter of her story points back to the same truth: God’s Word sustained her. Millie was only six weeks old when her father suffered severe burns to his legs from an explosion. Overnight, Millie’s mother found herself caring for a newborn and a toddler while tending to a husband who was facing a long and painful recovery. Life was uncertain, and every dollar mattered. Yet when Millie looks back on those difficult years, she doesn’t first remember hardship. She remembers the faith that was demonstrated. Every Sunday morning, Millie’s mother would reach into a small jar where she saved a few quarters and hand one to Millie and one to her sister before they left for church. The family didn’t have much, but her parents believed that honoring God was never dependent on how much they had. “We were taught to tithe,” Millie recalled. “To give to the Lord because of His goodness to us.” Long before Millie understood phrases like “stewardship” or “planned giving,” she was learning a lesson that would shape the rest of her life: Generosity isn’t born out of abundance; it grows from trusting the one who provides. See how God is using the generosity of one group of friends to impact Bible translation → The Scripture Millie Carried Through the Years As Millie grew older, that foundation of faith continued to guide her. She married a godly man, and they centered their efforts around family, teaching and serving others. Both were educators, and they poured themselves into the lives of children while also remaining deeply involved in their church and community. Together, the couple experienced the joys of raising a family. But they also walked through a devastating loss. While Millie was pregnant with their younger son, the couple’s 7-year-old daughter tragically died. It’s difficult to imagine the depth of grief that Millie endured. Through her pain, she turned to God and His Word for comfort. Even now, decades later, she is still anchored by the promises found in Scripture. One particular passage resonates with Millie deeply: You will keep in perfect peace all who trust in you, all whose thoughts are fixed on you! Trust in the LORD always, for the LORD GOD is the eternal Rock. — Isaiah 26:3-4 (NLT) For Millie, Scripture was what met her in her grief, strengthened her through suffering and continued to anchor and guide her throughout the next chapters of her life. This past Easter, Mille’s family experienced another tragic event — her son was involved in a head-on collision. Thankfully he survived but was hospitalized and treated for serious injuries. Millie believes the Lord’s presence was unmistakable in the moments that followed this event. A Gift Rooted in Gratitude Not long after her son’s accident, Millie received a mailing from Wycliffe Foundation that included information about charitable gift annuities. For Millie, this felt like an invitation and an opportunity to respond to God’s faithfulness through generosity. A charitable gift annuity was not a completely new concept to Millie. Through family members connected with Faith Comes By Hearing (a Wycliffe partner organization), she learned about this unique giving option and appreciated that it could provide her with a lifetime income while also supporting a ministry she cared deeply about. When she received the information about charitable gift annuities, she saw it as another opportunity to worship the Lord and express her gratitude for His protection and provision. Millie reached out to Wycliffe Foundation, and Michael Occhipinti, senior gift planning advisor, quickly connected with her. 是什么环境或经历决定了你的生活? 对于93岁的米莉(名字变了)来说,她的证词是被大萧条和严重损失所塑造的,但也是一种持久的信仰和一生目睹上帝的忠诚发展。 她的故事的每一章都指向同样的真理:上帝的话支撑了她.

米莉只有六个星期大,当她的父亲在爆炸中腿部严重烧伤。 一夜之间,米莉的母亲发现自己在照顾一个新生儿和幼儿,同时照顾一个面临长期痛苦康复的丈夫。 生活是不确定的,每一美元都很重要。 但当米莉回顾那些艰难的岁月时,

她记得所表现的信仰. 每周日早上,米莉的母亲会到达一个小罐子,在那里她保存了几分钱,在他们出发去教堂之前,将一张交给米莉,一张交给她的妹妹. 她的父母认为尊重上帝永远不取决于他们拥有多少。 米莉回忆说,“我们被教导了十分之一。”

以至报应我们的主。 早在米莉明白“偷窥”或“计划施舍”等短语之前,她就已经吸取了将塑造其余生的教训:慷慨并非由丰产而生;它从信任提供者而增长。

看上帝如何利用一群朋友的慷慨影响圣经的翻译 – 《圣经·米莉》在米莉变老的岁月里载着她,这种信仰的基础继续引导着她. 她嫁给了一个虔诚的人,他们围绕家庭,教学和为他人服务而集中了自己的努力.

两人都是教育工作者,他们投入到儿童生活中,同时也深入参与他们的教会和社区。 夫妇们一起经历了养育家庭的快乐. 但他们也经历了毁灭性的损失。 Milie怀了年幼的儿子,

很难想象米莉承受的悲痛有多深。 通过她的痛苦,她转而向上帝和上帝的话求慰. 即使现在,几十年之后,她仍然以圣经中的承诺为依托。 一个特别的段落与米莉深刻的共鸣:所有信任你的人,你都将在完美的和平中守住,他们的思想都固定在你身上!

相信耶和华,因为耶和华是永恒的磐石。 以赛亚26:3-4 (NLT)对米莉来说,圣经是她在悲痛中遇见她,通过苦难使她更加坚强,并继续支撑和引导她整个下半生。 过去复活节,米尔的家人经历了另一个悲惨事件——她的儿子卷入了一次正面碰撞.

幸好他幸存下来,但住院治疗严重受伤。 Milie认为,在事件发生之后的那一刻,上帝的出现是无可置疑的。 Millie在儿子出事不久后收到Wycliffe基金会的邮件,

对米莉来说,这感觉像是一次邀请和机会,通过慷慨回应上帝的忠诚. 慈善礼物年金对米莉来说并不是全新的概念.

她通过与Faith Comes Booth(一个Wycliffe伙伴组织)有关的家庭成员了解到这一独特的赠与选择,并意识到这一选择能为她提供终身收入,同时支持她深爱的部委。

当她收到有关慈善礼物年金的信息时,她认为这是又一次机会,可以崇拜主,并对他的保护和供养表示感谢. 米莉联系了威克利夫基金会,高级礼品规划顾问迈克尔·奥西平蒂(Michael Occhipinti)迅速与她联系. 在整个过程中,他在她祷告地考虑她的下一步时与她同行。

title: Making a Difference for Future Generations
source: Wycliffe Bible Translators · 译经故事
summary: See how Bible translation is transforming future generations as communities in Guatemala, Peru, Tanzania and Nigeria gain access to God’s Word in languages they clearly understand.   The post  Making a Difference for Future Generations  appeared first on  Wycliffe .
summary_zh: 了解圣经翻译如何改变后代，因为危地马拉、秘鲁、坦桑尼亚和尼日利亚的社区以他们清楚理解的语言获得神的话语。“Making a Difference for Future Generations”一文首次出现在Wycliffe上。
title_zh: 为子孙后代带来改变
content: How old were you when you first learned that Jesus loves you? Perhaps you’ve always known it and can’t remember a day when you didn’t know the song “Jesus Loves Me” or couldn’t recite John 3:16 by heart. Maybe you were a teenager and learned about Jesus’ love through a friend or church summer camp. Or were in college and went to a concert where the gospel was clearly articulated. Maybe you were in the trenches of the workforce, and a coworker boldly shared with you about the God who radically changed their life. Regardless of how old you were, each of us who has chosen to follow Jesus has an origin story — a moment in our lives when the knowledge that “Jesus loves me, this I know, for the Bible tells me so” moved from head knowledge to heart belief. And from then on, our lives were transformed forever. This is the truth of the gospel and the power of understanding that Jesus loves you. People around the world are discovering the personal truth of John 3:16 for themselves in a language and format they clearly understand. Explore why understanding that “God so loved the world” transforms entire communities → A Changing Reality Throughout Christian history, the gospel has spread from one community to the next. Stories were told and retold, Scripture was translated, churches were planted, and discipleship deepened as people learned more about Jesus. Bible translation is foundational to all ministries of the church. It fuels evangelism, church planting, discipleship and more. It equips people to move from a blurry picture of who God is to a clear understanding and personal encounter with Jesus as Lord. Through Scripture, people are able to read, hear or see the love of God on display. Just two decades ago, most of the world’s language communities still needed Bible translation work to begin , let alone be completed. But praise God, in the last few years, we’ve seen tremendous progress made, with Bible translation underway in more languages than ever before . While the change in numbers is exciting, what’s more important is what they signify: Every number represents a person who has a story that matters to God. For these communities, the stories of future generations are being completely rewritten as children will now grow up never remembering a day when they didn’t have access to God’s Word in a language and format they clearly understand. That statement bears repeating: There will now be people who never remember a day when they didn’t have access to God’s Word in a language and format they clearly understand. From the first word of Genesis to the last word of Revelation, the Bible tells one incredible story: God’s love for the world and His invitation for people from every nation and language to know Him. Get a glimpse of how God continues writing this story today as more and more people are experiencing the power of His Word. Watch the video → A New Generation Growing Up With God’s Word Let’s take a look at some of the recent communities that are experiencing not only life transformation but generational transformation as they encounter Jesus personally through Scripture. Jakalteko | Guatemala The Jakalteko Bible was dedicated in July 2026 in Guatemala! During the celebration, John 1:1-18 was read aloud — a passage that focuses on Christ, the eternal Word and our Redeemer. Early on, many women in the community memorized Job 19 . Like Job, they had faced various hardships in their lives and identified with his suffering. The book reminded them that God remains in control and that, in the midst of difficult circumstances, their Redeemer will deliver them and comfort them in their pain. Today, they have the full counsel of God’s Word and can now see this Redeemer fulfilled in Jesus in the New Testament. They are overjoyed that the Bible has arrived in the language they were born into! When the Bible was distributed, one mother who is raising her family alone said with joy and tears: “Thank God we have the Bible in our language. Now

title: Spoiled for Choice: Two New Graphic Novels of Pilgrim’s Progress
summary: Two new graphic novel adaptations of Pilgrim’s Progress have arrived within weeks of each other. Here's how they are similar and different, and my recommendation of which one to buy. See Also A La Carte (July 27) The Puritans: John Bunyan A La Carte (6/3)
summary_zh: 两部《天路历程》的全新漫画改编作品在相隔数周的时间内相继面世。以下是它们的异同之处，以及我对于购买哪一本的建议。另见《A La Carte》（7月27日）《清教徒：约翰·班扬》《A La Carte》（6月3日）
title_zh: 选择多多：两部全新《天路历程》绘本小说
content: I have often expressed how spoiled Christian readers are today. As if we needed more proof of this, how about the fact that in a single month, publishers released not one but two major graphic novel adaptations of Pilgrim’s Progress ? Both are well-written, beautifully illustrated, and faithful to Bunyan’s story. Let me help you understand their similarities and differences and tell you which one might be best to add to your library. Christian’s Quest is written by Tyler Van Halteren and illustrated by Manuel Zepic. It is published by Lithos Kids, which has already released the three-part Little Pilgrim’s Big Journey , an illustrated adaptation of Pilgrim’s Progress for young readers, and The Mansoul Chronicles , which is based on Bunyan’s Holy War . It is a 220-page 7×10.63 inch hardcover that targets children aged 8+, though it is meant to be enjoyed by teens and adults as well. Its illustrations are what I might describe as a clean, polished YA style. The lines are thin and tidy and much of the form comes from shading. The colors tend to maintain a soft, muted, painted look. It lightly updates some antiquated language so that Bunyan’s Slough of Despond becomes the Bog of Despond. Christian is youthful and fresh-faced, and his burden is a bulging pack on a frame. It includes some bonus material: a behind-the-scenes look at how a graphic novel is made, and a study guide that explains and applies each of the stages of Christian’s quest. It also indicates that a sequel, Christiana’s Crown , will be released in 2028. Pilgrim’s Progress: The Graphic Novel is written by Jeremy Patenaude, illustrated by Brent McKee, colored by Matt Wilson, and lettered by Taylor Esposito. It is published by Crossway as what I believe is the company’s first graphic novel, though it has a long history of publishing books for young readers. It is a 256-page 7×10.25 inch paperback that targets readers aged 14+. Its illustrations are what I might describe as gritty and stylized and perhaps a bit more indie than mainstream. It uses heavy brush ink, dark shadows, and vivid colors. It does not update Bunyan’s antiquated language. Christian is a gaunt, tormented, weathered adult whose burden is a huge stone roped to his back. Its bonus material includes a lexicon of the key characters and locations and reflections on each of the chapters. There is no indication of a sequel that will cover Christiana’s quest. While these two graphic novels tell the same story and tell it faithfully using dialogue and illustration rather than narration, they tell it using different visual language largely because Christian’s Quest is meant to be accessible to a younger demographic. You might say that Christian’s Quest is a bit more kid-friendly and Pilgrim’s Progress is a bit more adult-friendly, though both could easily be enjoyed by kids and adults alike. After all, who doesn’t enjoy reading the occasional graphic novel? Another key difference is that Pilgrim’s Progress is a paperback where Christian’s Quest is being sold as more of an heirloom object that features cloth binding, gold foil, and a ribbon marker. Let me show you a few examples of the art from each book. Christian’s Quest These are drawn from the publisher’s preview images. Pilgrim’s Progress These are drawn from the sample chapter on Crossway’s site. My Recommendation Which do I recommend? Either! Both! If your readers are younger, Christian’s Quest is the more obvious choice, and if they are older—teenagers and up—they may prefer Pilgrim’s Progress . But you couldn’t go wrong with either, and you couldn’t go wrong with picking up both. 我经常表达基督教读者今天是多么的被宠坏。 似乎我们需要更多的证据, 在一个月里, 出版商只发行了两部关于朝圣者进步的重要小说改编。 他们都写得很好,

让我来帮助你理解它们之间的相似之处和差异,并告诉你,哪一个可能最好加入你的图书馆. 由泰勒·范·哈特伦(英语:Tyler Van Halteren)撰写,曼努埃尔·泽皮奇(英语:Manuel Zepic)作画.

由Lithos Kids出版, 已经发行了三部曲小朝圣者大旅, 这是一项220页的7x10.63英寸硬盖,针对的是8岁以上儿童,但青少年和成年人也享受。

它的插图是我可以描述的 一种干净,光泽的YA风格。 线条细而整齐,形式大多来自阴影. 颜色倾向于保持柔软,沉默,绘画的外观. 它轻而易举地更新了一些古老的语言,使邦扬的"Despond的Slough"成为了Despond的Bog. 克里斯蒂安年轻又新面孔,他的担子是架子上的膨胀包.

包括一些奖品:一幅幕后小说是如何制作的,一幅研究指南解释并应用了基督教的追求的每个阶段。 这部续集《克里斯蒂安娜的王冠》将于2028年发行。

朝圣者的进步:图画小说由Jeremy Patenaude写作,布伦特·麦基(Brent Mckee)饰演,马特·威尔逊饰演,泰勒·埃斯波西托(Taylor Esposito)饰演. 由Crossway出版, 我认为这是公司的第一部平面小说, 它有256页7x10.25英寸的纸质背面,针对14岁以上读者。

它的插图是我可以说的 粗糙和结构化, 可能比主流多一点。 它使用重笔墨,暗影,以及生动的色彩. 它不会更新Bunyan的过时语言。 克里斯蒂安是一个胆小, 受折磨,风化的成年人, 他的负担是一个巨大的石头绑在背上。

它的奖金材料包括关键人物和地点的词汇表以及对每一章的思考. 没有迹象表明会续集克里斯蒂安娜的追求。

虽然这两部图画小说讲述了同一个故事,忠实地用对话和插图来讲述,而不是用不同的视觉语言讲述,这主要是因为克里斯蒂安的Quest本意是让年轻人口能够接触到.

基督教徒的追问更适合孩子, 朝圣者的进步更适合成年人, 毕竟,谁不喜欢偶尔读那本图画小说?

另一个关键区别是,朝圣者的进步是一个纸质的回扣,在那里,基督教的Quest被作为更多的继承物出售,该物的特点是布装、金瓦和丝带标志。 让我给你们看看每本书中的一些艺术例子。 基督教的追问 这些照片来自出版商的预览图像。

content: Tuesday is the day most publishers release their new books, so each week I like to let you know what has just come our way from the publishers I follow most closely. It is a quieter week than the last one, but it brings a revised edition of B. B. Warfield’s Biblical and Theological Studies, Alex Duke’s guided tour of Exodus (for which I provided a foreword), and two Crossway editions marking 500 years since William Tyndale’s English New Testament. On the academic side, you’ll find several noteworthy titles, including the New International Commentary on the Old Testament volume on Daniel 7–12. In each case, I’ve included the publisher’s description. Books for Everyone Zondervan From Silence to Sinai A Guided Tour of Exodus Alex Duke Publisher’s description What adjectives would you use to describe the Bible? Inspired. Amazing. Unique. Authoritative. Perfect. Pure. Life-changing. Those descriptions are all deserved. Your pastors and parents and Sunday School teachers were right. There’s no book like God’s Book. Here’s another adjective: confusing. The Bible can be confusing, especially certain parts of the Old Testament. Moments after coming across something inspiring and encouraging, you’ll read something that makes you wonder, What is even happening right now!? The book of Exodus is no exception. This sequel to Genesis begins with God’s surprising silence. What a stark contrast to Genesis, where God’s words set everything in motion. It then tells the story of God’s miraculous liberation of his people, complete with frogs falling from the sky and life-saving blood being painted over doorways. Finally, for the last half of the book, the action slows down as the people of God gather at the mountain of God to receive the Law of God in order to engage in the worship of God. From silence to Sinai, that’s the story of Exodus. To understand it all, most of us will need a guide. We’ll need some help. That’s what From Silence to Sinai is for. Alex Duke walks readers through the book of Exodus to show that nothing in God’s story is wasted—not the silence, not the ten signs, and not even the confusing parts. In Exodus, God is not absent, random, or unclear. He is revealing himself, redeeming his people, and teaching them how to live in his presence. Buy it at Amazon or Westminster Books . B&H The First Five Beating the Odds and Thriving as a Ministry Leader Kyle Worley and Joseph Worley Publisher’s description Is it possible to do more than survive in ministry leadership? Could you actually thrive? The alarming reality is that most ministry leaders will not make it more than five years in leadership. Burnout, lack of training, and an absence of coaches are all pitfalls on the road to sustainable ministry leadership. But there is a different roadmap for those willing to learn. In The First Five , Joseph and Kyle Worley present a pathway for thriving in ministry leadership. With over sixty years of experience, across churches of every size and shape, they provide a biblically rooted and tested approach to the personal, professional, and pastoral dynamics of ministry leadership. The First Five is designed to be a manual for new ministry leaders and those leading them. Don’t just read this book—use it! You can do more than survive as a ministry leader. You’ll also find Greg Gifford’s Lies My Therapist Told Me and several other titles. Recommended Reading Beer, Beef and Player’s Navy Cut. This is a brilliant article about C.S. Lewis and the vices that dogged him throughout his life—a three-pack-a day smoking habit, eating habits that bordered on gluttony, and far more alcohol than anyone should consume. “In case you really are new here and you mostly know Lewis from the kid’s books, let’s state the obvious: the man we universally honor as one of the 20th Century’s great saints smoked, ate and drank like he was a sponsored athlete of consumption. He sinned frequently through overindulgence. What do we do with this information?” How to Graciously Say No. You have probably run into the same conclusion I have: it’s often far harder to say no than to say yes. Yet sometimes the best thing we can do for ourselves and for others is to say no. Reagan Rose offers some thoughts on that (for those who have the ability to say no, of course, since in many occupations saying no isn’t an option). Can’t You Let Me Just Attend? “We live in a chronically noncommittal society. No wonder, then, that this has been dubbed the age of anxiety. J.V. Fesko makes a simple but wise point here: everyone doesn’t respond to preaching the same way. content: This week, the blog is sponsored by Moody Publishers and adapted from The Unstoppable Gospel by Karl Clauson. It’s impossible to disciple lost people. That sounds obvious. Maybe too obvious to even say out loud. But when the church dilutes or neglects the good news, devastation is left in its wake. After forty years of ministry, this is the most sobering truth I’ve learned about the Western church: We do not merely have a discipleship problem today. We have a gospel problem. Before we ever became weak at disciple-making, we began redefining conversion itself. We slowly traded supernatural regeneration for human decision. Salvation became a prayer to repeat, a card to sign, an aisle to walk, while millions were assured of heaven without ever being transformed by the power of God. We didn’t offer them a belief lacking power, we offered them a powerless belief. The result is a generation that has been deeply Christianized but not necessarily changed. They know the language. They know the songs. They know when to stand, when to sit, when to say amen. They have been immersed in church culture, yet many have never been brought from death to life. We have filled churches with people who have learned how to function in and around “Christianity” without ever truly following Christ. And when that happens, discipleship collapses under the weight of human effort. When evangelism centers on human decision, discipleship inevitably becomes self-powered. Following Jesus is reduced to behavior management, moral striving, and “try harder next time.” The supernatural life Christ promised is replaced with self-help dressed up in religious garb. Dallas Willard spoke of “the Great Omission,” the church’s failure to make disciples. He was right. But I believe something even deeper has happened. Before we omitted discipleship, we compromised the very gospel that births disciples in the first place. That is the crisis. That is the great deception. And until we recover the true faith that changes everything, we will continue trying to disciple people who have never truly been made alive. We have, sitting in our church chairs and pews every weekend—even in good, Bible-teaching churches—vast numbers of people who believe themselves to be saved but possess no power beyond their own efforts and whose lives show only surface evidence of new birth. People assume what they have is all God has for them, not knowing they are cultural Christians, so close yet so far from God. People who have been taught a version of Christianity divorced from repentance, from surrender, from the cost of discipleship and, tragically, from the power that makes the gospel unstoppable. Many profess Christ but don’t possess Christ. We’ve left people needing more, wanting more, and settling for too little. The great deception must end. There is life for the spiritually dead. There is surrender that leads to life instead of loss. There is repentance that produces the rhythm of a flourishing soul. There is discipline that flows from grace instead of fear or performance. And there is deep, liberating, unmistakable freedom when Christ becomes everything. This is why truth must be championed. Not as an idea, but as a reality that cuts, clarifies, and calls us forward. Because when truth becomes really clear, it doesn’t just inform you. It changes you. It brings you out of the fog, out of the confusion, out of the illusion—and into a life that is grounded, whole, and fully alive with God. This is the gospel that birthed the early church. This is the gospel that turned the world upside down. This is the gospel that sustains God’s kids under brutal persecution today. This is the gospel the church has forgotten and the good news it desperately needs. This is the gospel that still changes everything today. Learn more about how we’ve embraced a version of the gospel that falls short of the life Jesus promised, and how you can go from powerless belief to a true faith that changes everything. Get
content_zh:
博客由Mody出版社赞助, 门徒不可能失去人 这听起来很明显。 也许太明显了,甚至不能大声说出来。 但当教堂淡化或忽略了好消息时,毁灭就留在了它的后面.

这是40年的牧师, 我们今天不只是有门徒问题。 我们有一个福音问题。 在做门徒之前,我们开始重新定义皈依本身。 我们慢慢地用超自然再生来换取人类的决定。

救世主成为了重复的祷告,签字的名片,行走的走道,而数百万人则得到天堂的保证,永远没有被上帝的力量所改变. 我们并没有给他们一个没有权力的信仰, 其结果是一代人被深深地基督教化,但不一定改变. 他们知道语言。 他们知道歌曲。

他们知道何时可以站起,何时可以坐起,何时可以说阿门. 他们被浸入了教会文化中,然而许多人从未被从死亡中带入生命. 我们向教会灌输了那些学会如何在 " 基督教 " 内和周围运作而不真正遵循基督的人。 当这种情况发生时,门徒们在人类努力的重压下崩溃了.

当福音会以人类的决定为中心时,门徒不可避免地会变得自强自强. 追随耶稣被贬为行为管理、道德努力和“下次更努力”的人。 基督所承诺的超自然生命被取而代之的是身穿宗教外衣的自救. Dallas Willard谈到了教会未能培养出门徒的“大意念”。 他说得对。

但我相信发生了更深层的事 在我们忽略了门徒身份之前,我们破坏了出生的门徒们最初的福音。 这就是危机。 这是伟大的欺骗。 直到我们恢复改变一切的真正信仰之前,我们将继续尝试向从未真正被活生生地培养出来的门徒.

我们每个周末都坐在教堂的椅子上和教堂的树上,即使是好的,也是圣经教学的教堂。 我们有许多人相信自己是被拯救的,但除了自己的努力之外没有权力,他们的生活只显示新出生的表面证据。 人们猜想自己拥有的只是上帝给他们的一切,他们不知道自己是文化上的基督徒,所以距离上帝还相去甚远.

曾被教过基督教的人脱离了忏悔、投降、门徒费用以及可悲的使福音无法被阻止的力量。 许多人信奉基督, 我们让人们需要更多,需要更多, 伟大的欺骗必须结束。 精神上死去的人有生命

投降导致生命而不是损失。 有悔过感产生出一个繁荣的灵魂的节奏. 纪律是从优雅而不是恐惧或表现中产生的。 当基督变成一切时,有深刻的,解放的,不可磨灭的自由. 这就是为什么必须捍卫真理。 不是作为一个想法,而是作为一个现实,削减、澄清和召唤我们前进。

因为当真相变得非常清楚时, 它改变了你。 它使你从雾中、从迷惑中、从幻觉中、从幻觉中、从幻觉中、从幻觉中、从幻觉中、从幻觉中、从幻觉中、从幻觉中、从幻觉中、从幻觉中、从幻觉中、从幻觉中、从幻觉中、从幻觉中、从幻觉中、从幻觉中、从幻觉中、从幻觉中、从幻觉中、从幻觉中、从幻觉中、从幻雾中、从幻觉中、从幻觉中、从幻觉中、从幻觉中、从幻觉中、从幻觉中、从幻觉中、从幻觉中、从幻觉中、从幻觉中、从幻觉中、从幻觉中、从幻觉中、从幻觉中、从幻觉中、从幻幻觉中、从幻幻觉中、从幻幻出出,进入一个与神同活生。 这是诞生早期教堂的福音. 这就是使世界颠倒的福音。

这是上帝孩子今天遭受残酷迫害的福音。 这是教堂被遗忘的福音 也是它急需的好消息 这是今天仍然改变一切的福音。

author: Tim Challies

title: Arrested at the hospital where he worked, he turned the prison into a pulpit
summary: 🇪🇷Eritrea· 2010s
summary_zh: 🇪🇷厄立特里亚·21世纪10年代
title_zh: 他在自己工作的医院被捕，并将监狱变成了讲坛。
content: Dr Berhane was a new believer in Jesus, working in a hospital in Eritrea, when the secret police came for him. His crime was his faith. They put him in prison for eleven months, in one of the harshest systems on earth, a place designed to make Christians disappear and go quiet. He did the opposite. "Every day I was clapping my hands," he said, "and prisoners would come forward and I shared the gospel." A man who had only recently met Jesus decided his cell was simply the next place to introduce Him. Three Bibles and a valley of death The authorities took his Bible. He smuggled another in. They took that one too, and he smuggled a third. He leaned hard on the Psalms, and when fellow prisoners were taken out and executed, the old line about walking through the valley of the shadow of death stopped being poetry and became the thing that held him upright. Eleven months of that did not break him. It made him a preacher. The guards meant to silence a new Christian and instead handed him a congregation with nowhere to go. Wherever they put you, Jesus goes with you, and He is not intimidated by the walls. Dr Berhane found that out in an Eritrean prison. You can trust it wherever you are.
content_zh:
Berhane博士是耶稣的新信徒,在厄立特里亚的一家医院工作,当时秘密警察来找他。 他的罪行是他的信仰。 他们把他关进监狱11个月,在地球上最严酷的系统之一,一个旨在使基督徒消失和安静的地方. 他做的恰恰相反。

"每天我拍手,"他说:"囚犯会站出来,我分享福音". 一个刚认识耶稣的人决定 他的牢房只是下一个介绍他的地方 三个圣经和一个死亡之谷 当局拿走了他的圣经。 他又偷渡进来了 他们也拿走了那个 他走私了三分之一

他极力倚靠"诗经",当狱友被带出处死时,关于走过死亡阴影谷的老台词不再是诗歌,成为了扶他站直的东西. 11个月没有打倒他。 这让他成了传教士。 守卫们打算让新基督徒安静下来,反而给了他一个无处可去的会众.

无论他们把你放在哪里,耶稣都跟着你,他不受墙壁的恐吓. Berhane博士在厄立特里亚的一所监狱发现了这一点。 你可以相信它 无论你在哪里。

title: A construction engineer in Madagascar became convinced the Bible was true
summary: 🇲🇬Madagascar· 2013
summary_zh: 🇲🇬马达加斯加·2013年
title_zh: 一位在马达加斯加的建筑工程师确信圣经是真的
content: Melias was building things for a living in Madagascar, a construction engineer with a steady trade and, by his own account, no particular expectation that God would interrupt him. In 2013, at twenty-one, God did. It was not dramatic thunder. It was quieter and harder to argue with. "The Holy Spirit convinced my heart that the Bible is true," Melias said. "I found new joy and excitement learning about Jesus through the Scriptures." The book he might have dismissed became the most alive thing in his life. From building houses to building the church He could have kept his new faith as a private comfort and gone on with engineering. Instead he gave it everything. In 2015 he trained for six months as a missionary, and since then he has planted churches and discipled new believers among the Tanala people in Ikongo and the Sakalava in Nosy Be, some of the least reached corners of the island. Now he is training three more Malagasy missionaries to do the same. Madagascar is not a footnote in what God is doing. He is raising up local people like Melias, engineers and tradesmen and ordinary workers, and sending them to their own unreached neighbours. When the Holy Spirit convinces your heart that this is all true, it does not stay a hobby. It becomes the thing you build your life around. He is ready to convince yours.
content_zh:
梅利亚斯在马达加斯加为生计而建东西,他是一位稳定的建筑工程师,据他自己说,他并不特别期望上帝会打断他。 2013年,21时,上帝做到了. 这不是戏剧性的雷声。 更安静,更难争论 "圣灵使我的心相信圣经是真的,"梅利亚斯说.

"我发现新的快乐和兴奋 通过圣经学习耶稣。" 他可能放弃的书 成为他一生中最活的 从建房到建教堂 他本可以保持他作为私人慰藉的新信仰,继续从事工程工作. 相反,他给了它一切。

2015年,他作为传教士接受了半年的训练,此后他在伊孔戈的塔纳拉人和诺西贝的萨卡拉瓦人中种植了教堂和门徒新信徒,其中部分到达的岛角最少. 现在他正在训练另外三名马达加斯加传教士, 马达加斯加不是上帝所作所为的一个脚注。

他正在培养梅利亚斯,工程师和商人以及普通工人等当地人,并将他们送到他们自己无法接触到的邻居那里. 当圣灵说服你的心脏 这一切都是真的, 它不仍然是爱好。 它成为你围绕你生活的东西。 他准备说服你

title: A New Testament sat in his welding workshop until a teenager finally read it
summary: 🇳🇪Agadez· 2000s
summary_zh: 🇳🇪阿加德兹·21世纪初
title_zh: 一本新约圣经一直放在他的焊接车间里，直到一位少年终于读了它。
content: Someone left a New Testament in Pierre's welding workshop in Niger, and for a while it just sat there. He was a teenager, and eventually he picked it up. What he read did not match what he had been told about Christians. It was full of tenderness, of nearness to the poorest, exactly the kind of world his young heart had been quietly hoping was real. Years later he moved to Agadez, out toward the desert, and there he found the thing the book had described. A church family drawn from Benin, Togo, Burkina Faso, France, and Niger, living out what he had only read about. No regret, not for a single day Pierre became a lay missionary, and he does not hedge when he talks about it. "I have never regretted converting to the Christian faith," he says, "not even for a single day." That is a bold thing to say in Niger, where jihadist groups make following Jesus dangerous and his own children have stayed Muslim, something he carries with love and without pressure. Still, no regret. Not one day. He read about a God who is tender toward the poor, and he found that God to be exactly as advertised. Whatever you have heard about Jesus secondhand, He holds up when you finally meet Him yourself. Pierre would tell you to open the book and see.
content_zh:
有人在尼日尔的皮埃尔焊接车间留下了一份新约, 他少年时期,最终他捡到了. 他所读的内容与他被告知的基督徒的情况不符。 它充满了温柔,与最贫穷的人的亲近, 正是他年轻时所希望的世界是真实的。

多年后,他搬到阿加德兹, 向着沙漠, 在那里他发现了书上描述的东西。 一个来自贝宁、多哥、布基纳法索、法国和尼日尔的教会家庭,靠他只读过的东西生活。 没有遗憾,没有一天,皮埃尔成为了一名非专业的传教士,他谈论这件事时不设套.

"我从未后悔过皈依基督教信仰",他说:"即使是一天也没有". 在尼日尔,这是一件大胆的事,在那里,圣战团体追随耶稣,而他自己的孩子则留在穆斯林手中,他带着爱,没有压力。 不过,没有遗憾。 一日不见.

他曾诵读了真主--对于贫民是温和的--他发现真主确是彻知的。 无论你听到什么关于耶稣的二手消息 当你们终于亲眼见到他时 他都挺过来了 Pierre会告诉你打开书看看

title: He was taught Christians do not pray. Then he watched his uncle pray before a meal
title_zh: 他被教导说基督徒不祷告。然后，他看到叔叔在饭前祷告。
content: Charles Yabaga Diarra grew up in a strict Muslim family in Lere, Mali, where Christians were mocked and misunderstood. His father, a headmaster and politician, ran the house like a school. As a boy, Charles fled about a hundred and fifty miles to stay with an uncle, and there he ran straight into something he had been told did not exist. His uncle, a Christian pastor, bowed his head and prayed before the meal. Charles was stunned. "Because we are Christians, we pray before meals," the uncle explained. Charles had been taught that Christians do not pray at all. That simple prayer, in his own language, lodged in him and would not leave. Just show me the way His father pulled him back and forced him into Quranic school, but the seed was planted. Years later, back with his uncle, tired and searching, Charles finally prayed his own prayer. "Lord, I'm really tired of seeking the truth. Just show me the way." A verse he had heard at a Vacation Bible School came back to him, and in November 1981 he gave his life to Jesus. The cost has been real. Charles is a preacher now, displaced by Mali's conflict and facing daily pressure. But he did not go alone. Of his fourteen siblings, most now follow Jesus, and around a hundred Christians gather at his extended family events. One uncle praying over dinner turned a whole family toward Jesus. Your quiet, ordinary faithfulness may be planting more than you know.
content_zh:
查尔斯·亚巴加·迪亚拉(Charles Yabaga Diarra)在马里勒尔一个严格的穆斯林家庭长大,在那里基督徒受到嘲笑和误解. 他的父亲是一名校长和政治家,他像学校一样管理着房子. 童年时,查尔斯逃离了大约一百五十英里,与一个叔叔住在一起,在那里,他直接遇到了他被告知的东西并不存在.

他的叔叔,一位基督教牧师,低头祷告,在饭前祷告. 查尔斯被惊呆了 "因为我们是基督徒,我们吃饭前祈祷",叔叔解释道. 查尔斯被告知基督徒根本不祷告 用他自己的语言祈祷,他不会离开。

只要告诉我他父亲把他拉回来的方式 强迫他进入古兰经学校 但种子是种的 多年之后,与他的叔叔一起回来,疲惫和寻找,查尔斯终于自己祈祷. "主啊,我真的厌倦了寻找真相. "给我带路" 他在一所假期圣经学校听到的一首诗回到了他身边,1981年11月他把生命献给了耶稣.

代价是真实的。 查尔斯现在是一名传教士,因马里的冲突而流离失所,每天都面临压力。 但他没有一个人去。 他的十四个兄弟姐妹中,大多数现在都跟随耶稣,大约一百名基督徒聚集在他的大家庭活动中. 一个叔叔为晚餐祷告 整个家庭都向耶稣倾斜 你安静的,普通的忠诚 可能是种更多 比你知道。

title: He found a Bible in a secondhand shop and thought he was the only Christian in Yemen
summary: 🇾🇪Yemen· 2000s
summary_zh: 🇾🇪也门·21世纪初
title_zh: 他在一家二手商店里找到了一本圣经，以为自己是也门唯一的基督徒。
content: Mohammad grew up in Yemen, in a conservative Muslim home, in a country with almost no visible church at all. About seventeen years ago he found a Bible in a secondhand shop. He took it home and read it in hiding, because being caught with it could cost him everything. What he read pulled him in, and he gave his life to Jesus. Then came a strange loneliness. "When I came to faith, I thought I was the only believer in Yemen," he said. "For a long time, I didn't know any other Yemeni Christians." He was never actually alone He was wrong about being alone, and God kept proving it. Mohammad and his wife Alima, who came to Jesus after reading the Gospels herself, had been unable to have children for seven years. They prayed, and the infertility ended. Once, in a car accident, Mohammad says he saw a white light in the shape of a cross. Slowly he found other Yemeni believers, received discipleship, and today helps lead a house church in one of the hardest places on earth to follow Jesus. The man who thought he was the only one is now helping build a family of them. If you feel like the only believer in your world, take heart. Jesus is already gathering people you have not met yet, and He has not left you on your own.
content_zh:
默罕默德成长于也门,在一个保守的穆斯林家庭,在一个几乎完全没有可见教堂的国家. 大约十七年前,他在二手店里发现了一本圣经. 他带回家藏起来读,因为被抓到会损失一切. 他读到的东西把他拉进来 他把生命交给耶稣 然后出现了奇怪的孤独

"当我回到信仰中,我以为我是也门唯一的信徒,"他说. "很久以来,我不认识其他也门基督徒". 他从不孤单 他不该独自一人 上帝一直在证明 默罕默德和他的妻子阿利玛在亲自阅读福音书后来到耶稣身边,已经无法生育7年. 他们祈祷,不孕症结束。

有一次,在一次车祸中,默罕默德说看到十字架形状的白光. 他慢慢地找到了其他也门信徒,获得了门徒资格,今天帮助带领一所位于地球上最难的地方的房屋教堂追随耶稣. 认为自己是唯一一个的人 现在正在帮助他们建立一个家庭。 如果你觉得自己是世上唯一相信的人,请记住。

耶稣已经聚集了你们尚未认识的人,他没有离开你们。

title: A widow heard the good news from a travelling salesman and could not unhear it
summary: Laos· 2022
title_zh: 一位寡妇从一位推销员那里听到了好消息，从此念念不忘。
content: Pei was a fifty-two-year-old widow in Laos, raised the way her whole village was raised, worshipping ancestors and local spirits in a place where the government pushes atheism and neighbours warn that following the God of foreigners will offend the gods of home. Then a salesman came through and, somewhere between selling his goods, told her about Jesus. Salvation as a gift, not a payment. Pei believed it. She let go of the ancestor worship she had carried her whole life and quietly followed Jesus instead. The cost at her own front door She was discipled in secret for four months, growing strong enough to speak. The first people she told were her daughter and her son-in-law, who happens to be a policeman. They did not celebrate. He threatened her, saying that if she did not stop believing in Jesus, they would report her, jail her, or throw her out. In June they made good on it, tossing her clothes into the yard and telling her to go live with the people who gave her this Jesus. She went. She did not go back. A widow with nothing chose Jesus over a roof, because she had found something no one could evict from her heart. Following Jesus is not always safe, but it is always worth it. What Pei found is worth more than what it cost her, and it is offered to you too.
content_zh:
裴 was在老挝是一位52岁的寡妇,养大了整个村庄的养殖方式,在政府推崇无神论的地方崇拜祖先和地方灵灵,邻居警告说,追随外国人神会冒犯家乡神灵. 然后一个推销员走过来,在出售他的商品之间,告诉她耶稣的事. 救世是礼物,不是报酬

裴 believed信之. 她放弃了她毕生怀念的祖先的崇拜,悄悄地跟随耶稣. 在她自己的前门付出的代价 她被秘密地关了四个月, 变得足够强大,可以说话。 她告诉的第一个人是她的女儿和女婿,她们碰巧是一名警察。 他们没有庆祝。

他威胁她,说如果她不停止相信耶稣,他们会告发她,监禁她,或者把她赶出去. 6月,他们在上面做得很好,把她的衣服扔到院子里,并告诉她去和给她这个耶稣的人一起生活. 她去了 她去了吗? 她没有回去。 一个什么都没有的寡妇选择了耶稣 而不是一个屋顶, 因为她已经发现了一些没人能从她的心脏里赶走的东西。

追随耶稣并不总是安全的,但总是值得的. 裴氏发现的比付出的代价更值钱,也是献给你的.

title: After his daughter was killed, he prayed for a Bible no one could take from him
summary: Uzbekistan and Tajikistan· 2020s
summary_zh: 乌兹别克斯坦和塔吉克斯坦·2020年代
title_zh: 女儿被杀后，他祈祷能拥有一本无人能夺走的圣经
content: Rashid Kadirov was a Muslim in Central Asia when the worst thing happened. His six-year-old daughter Azizza was killed by a drunk neighbour driving a tractor. In his grief he went looking for something the ache could rest on, and he went to the Koran. There he read a line, in Surah 5:70, that pointed back to the Gospels as holy scripture. So he prayed a strange, specific prayer. He asked God for an Injil, a New Testament. His friends brought him one. It was a stolen Gideon Bible, taken from a vandalised car. It did not last. When the friends took it back, Rashid prayed again, this time for a Bible no one could take away from him. The book that stayed Then a couple arrived from Tajikistan, sent by a former classmate of his who had himself come to Christ. They carried a Bible and a copy of the JESUS Film. Rashid and his wife Aleka watched it, and as the good news was explained, each of them, without telling the other, quietly prayed to receive Jesus. Aleka barely understood it all. "She had very little understanding of the Gospel," she said later, "and yet peace flooded her heart." They were baptised in Tajikistan, and Rashid started telling others what he had found. A grieving father asked for a book, and God gave him a Person. The peace Rashid could not manufacture arrived the moment Jesus did. He is close to the brokenhearted, and He is near to you.
content_zh:
拉希德·卡迪罗夫(Rashid Kadirov)是中亚穆斯林,当时最糟糕的事情发生了. 他的六岁女儿Azizza被驾拖拉机喝醉的邻居杀死. 在悲痛中,他去寻找可以安息的东西,他去了可兰经. 在那里,他读到了一行,在苏拉5:70中,指向福音书作为圣经. 所以他祈祷了一个奇怪的,具体的祈祷.

他向上帝祈求"印吉尔","新约". 他的朋友给他带来了一个。 是一辆被偷来的吉迪恩圣经 从被破坏的汽车上拍下来的 它没有持续。 当朋友们收回它时,拉希德再次祈祷,这次要一本圣经,没有人能夺走他. 留下来的书 之后一对夫妇从塔吉克斯坦赶来,他们是由自己来到基督的前同学派来的.

他们携带了圣经和JESUS电影的拷贝. 拉希德和他的妻子阿莱卡观看了,正如好消息被解释的那样,他们每个人都在不告诉对方的情况下悄悄地祈祷要接受耶稣. 阿莱卡根本不懂这些

"她对福音几乎没有什么了解,"后来她说,"然而和平却淹没了她的心. 他们在塔吉克斯坦接受洗礼,拉希德开始告诉其他人他发现了什么. 一个悲伤的父亲要求一本书,上帝给了他一个人. 和平拉希德无法在耶稣到达的时候制造。 他与心碎者密不可分,他与你们密不可分。

title: 35 priests could not help her. In a church she saw Jesus crush what was choking her
summary: 🇱🇰North Central Province· 2021
summary_zh: 北中央省
title_zh: 35位神父都无法帮助她。在教堂里，她看到耶稣粉碎了正在扼住她喉咙的东西。
content: Chandra lived in a rural village in Sri Lanka's North Central Province, and she was slowly falling apart. Pain, weakness, a heart that raced for no reason doctors could name. She and her family were Hindu, so they did what they knew to do. They went to priest after priest. Thirty-five of them. Nothing changed. In July 2021 they walked into a church instead. As people prayed for her, Chandra saw something. Demons were trying to strangle her, and then Jesus Christ stepped in and stamped on them. She felt the pain and the sickness drain out of her body as they were defeated. In the vision Jesus spoke Scripture over her, from Psalm 34. "They looked to Him and were radiant," He said, and told her she would be radiant too if she trusted Him. The prayer a father prayed Her husband Dinesh, a day labourer, watched his wife come back to life and made God a promise. "God, if you will heal my wife, I will dedicate my daughter for your service." The whole family, who had barely heard the name of Jesus, gave their lives to Him. Their daughter Tenusha told her class what had happened, that her mother was free and that Jesus forgives sinners and makes them new. They did not keep it to themselves. A house church started in their home with four people. By now it is forty-six. Jesus is still stronger than whatever is choking the life out of you. He steps in, He stamps it down, and He calls you radiant.
content_zh:
钱德拉住在斯里兰卡中北部省的一个乡村,她慢慢地分崩离析. 痛苦,软弱,一个无缘无故的心脏 医生无法命名 她和她的家人是印度教徒,所以他们做了他们知道的事。 他们跟随牧师去了牧师那里. 三十五门. 什么都没有改变。 2021年7月,他们走进了一座教堂。

当人们为她祈祷时,钱德拉看到了一些东西. 恶魔试图掐死她,然后耶稣基督介入并盖在他们身上. 她感到痛苦和疾病 排出她的身体 当他们被打败。 在视觉中,耶稣说圣经 超过她,从Psalm 34。 他说:他们崇拜他,而且赞颂他超绝万物。他说:她也超绝万物,如果她信任他。

一个父亲祈祷她的丈夫迪尼什(Dinesh),一个白天的劳工,看着他的妻子复活,并给上帝一个承诺. "上帝,如果你能治愈我的妻子, 我将奉献我的女儿为你服务。" 几乎听不到耶稣之名的全家都为他献出了生命.

他们的女儿特努沙告诉了班上所发生的事情,她的母亲是自由的,耶稣宽恕了罪人,使他们成为新人. 他们没有保守秘密。 一所房屋教堂在他们家中开始,共有4人. 时已四十六. 耶稣仍然比任何 扼杀你生命的东西更强大 他走进来,他把它印下来,他叫你光辉。

title: He prayed for his mother's infected leg. Then his Muslim neighbours started coming
summary: 🇸🇩El Hasahisa· 2022
summary_zh: 🇸🇩哈萨希萨·2022年
title_zh: 他为母亲感染的腿祈祷。然后，他的穆斯林邻居开始前来
content: Pastor Abdalla Haron Sulieman gathered his small church in El Hasahisa, Sudan, to pray for his mother. Aisha Adam was sixty, and a leg infection had worn her down. They prayed, and she recovered. What looked like a private family mercy did not stay private for long. Word of the healing moved through the town, which is mostly Muslim. And people started showing up at the church. Not to argue. To ask if the God who healed Aisha might heal them too. When a healing becomes a door That is exactly the kind of thing that makes some people afraid. Local extremists pressed the police to arrest Sulieman, and they did, charging him under an old law with claiming to be a witch doctor, as if the love of Jesus were a kind of sorcery. Believers across Sudan shared his name and called for his release. "This is a serious violation against Christians in Sudan," said one, an evangelist named Francis Ismail. But notice what the fear could not undo. A mother was well. A Muslim town had seen the name of Jesus do something real, and neighbours who had never entered a church walked in looking for Him. God still heals, and He still uses one ordinary answered prayer to open a door no one can shut. He can open one where you are too.
content_zh:
Abdalla Haron Sulieman牧师在苏丹El Hasahisa聚集了他的小教堂,为其母亲祈祷。 艾莎·亚当六十岁 腿部感染使她疲惫不堪 他们祈祷,她恢复了。 看起来像一个私人家庭的怜悯 并没有长期保持私人。 关于治愈的传言传遍了大部分是穆斯林的城镇。 人们开始出现在教堂。 不为辩才.

问治愈艾莎的神能否治愈他们 当治愈变成一扇门 这正是那种让人害怕的东西。 当地的极端分子逼迫警察逮捕苏利曼,他们确实如此,根据旧法指控他自称巫医,仿佛对耶稣的爱是一种巫术.

苏丹各地的信徒都认同他的名字,要求释放他。 "这是对苏丹基督徒的严重侵犯",一位名叫弗朗西斯·伊斯梅尔的福音者说. 但请注意恐惧无法消除 一个母亲很好 一个穆斯林城镇看到了耶稣的名字做一些真实的事情,从未进入教堂的邻居走进教堂寻找他.

上帝仍然痊愈,他仍然使用一个普通的应答祷告来打开一个没人能关闭的门. 他可以打开一个你的地方。

title: Karma said he had to earn heaven. At 17 he heard he could be forgiven
summary: Rakiraki· 1990s
summary_zh: 拉基拉基·1990年代
title_zh: 因果报应说他必须修功德才能上天堂。17岁时，他听说自己可以得到宽恕。
content: Simon Gounder was born into a strict Hindu family in Fiji. His great-grandfather had been shipped from India as a contract labourer after the British took the islands in 1874, and the family settled in a small village in the north of Viti Levu. Simon grew up inside a system with clear rules. "As a Hindu, we believed in karma," he said. "If you do good karma, you get to heaven. If you do bad karma, you will be punished." It was a ledger he could never quite balance. He knew his own wrongs too well. The night the ledger closed At seventeen, a friend invited him to a Christian youth meeting in another town. There he heard something that did not fit anything he had been taught. That Jesus Christ could simply forgive sins. Not offset them, not average them out over lifetimes. Forgive them. Simon felt the weight of his own failures and, for the first time, an offer to be free of them. "I gave my life to Jesus that night," he said. He hid it from his parents at first. When they found out, they were not happy. But the son who came home changed did not stop there. In time he led his whole family to Christ, and he went on to plant a ministry that carries the same forgiveness to others. Karma keeps a running tab you can never clear. Jesus tears the tab up. Whatever you are carrying tonight, He is still in the business of forgiving it all at once.
content_zh:
西蒙·古德出生于斐济一个严格的印度教家庭. 他的曾祖父在1874年英国人攻占群岛后,作为合同工从印度被运走,全家定居在维提莱武北部的一个小村庄. 西蒙在一个有明确规则的系统中长大. "作为一个印度教徒,我们相信因果报应,"他说. "若作善因缘即得上天.

若作恶报果报果报果. " 这是他无法平衡的分类账 他对自己的错误太了解了 结账的那一晚 17岁时,一位朋友邀请他到另一个城镇的一次基督教青年会议. 在那里,他听到一些不符合他所教过的东西。 耶稣基督可以宽恕罪过

不抵消它们, 也不平均出一生。 原谅他们 西蒙感受到了自己失败的轻重,并首次提出摆脱这些失败. "当晚我把生命交给耶稣,"他说. 起初他瞒着父母 当他们发现, 他们不高兴。 但回家的儿子变了 并没有停下来。

时他带领全家来到基督身边,他继续栽培一个对别人同样怀有宽恕的部. 卡玛一直有追踪器 你永远无法清除 耶稣撕开标签。 无论你今晚携带什么 他现在仍然要马上原谅这一切

title: You can kill me, but you cannot take my faith in Jesus
summary: 🇧🇩Bangladesh· 2021-2022
title_zh: 你可以杀了我，但你不能夺走我对耶稣的信仰
content: Nur Alam and Afzal Hosen left Islam to follow Jesus in 2021, and they were baptised soon after. They did not keep it quiet. They wanted the Muslim community they came from to know the Jesus they had found, so they handed out Bibles and booklets around their part of Bangladesh. That is when the trouble started. A group seized Nur and locked him in a room for thirty hours, no food, no water, no sleep, demanding he return to Islam and threatening to kill him and his family. He would not bend. "At some point during the interrogation," Nur said, "they became hopeless, seeing my strong faith in Jesus." A faith they could not confiscate Days after Nur was freed, they came for Afzal. They beat him and accused him of being paid to convert. His answer has the ring of the early church about it. "You can kill me," he told them, "but you cannot take my faith in the Lord Jesus away from me." Both men were released, bruised and exhausted and still standing. They had discovered the thing every threat runs into eventually. You can take a man's freedom, his comfort, even his life, but the faith Jesus plants in a heart is not yours to seize. If Jesus is worth that to two young men in Bangladesh, He is worth your whole life too.
content_zh:
努尔·阿拉姆(Nur Alam)和阿夫扎尔·霍森(Afzal Hosen)于2021年离开伊斯兰教跟随耶稣,他们不久就接受了洗礼. 他们没有保持沉默。 他们希望来自他们的穆斯林社区了解他们找到的耶稣,于是他们散发了他们所在的孟加拉国地区的圣经和小册子. 这就是问题开始的时候。

一群人抓住努尔,把他锁在一个房间里30小时,没有食物,没有水,没有睡眠,要求他返回伊斯兰教,并威胁要杀死他和他的家人. 他不会弯腰的 "在审讯期间的某个时候,"努尔说:"他们变得无望,看到我对耶稣的强烈信仰". 努尔解放后,他们无法没收信仰,他们来到阿夫扎尔。

他们殴打他,并指控他被收钱皈依。 他的答案是早期教会的戒指 他对他们说:你们可以杀我,但你们不能夺走我对主耶稣的信仰。 两人被释放,伤痕累累,仍然站立. 他们发现了每个威胁最终都遇到的东西

你可以拿一个人的自由,他的舒适,甚至他的生命, 但是信仰耶稣植根于一个心脏 不是你的夺取。 如果耶稣对孟加拉国的两个年轻人来说是值得的,那么他也值得你一辈子。

title: A soldier who should have died in battle walked into a demon's shrine
summary: 🇲🇲Myanmar· 2010s
title_zh: 一名本应死于战斗的士兵走进了恶魔的神殿
content: Pastor Dano was a soldier before he was a pastor. He came out of the battlefield alive when he had no reason to, and he never shook the sense of why. "I believe God preserved my life from death on the battlefield for a purpose," he said. The purpose showed up in a Buddhist village that wanted nothing to do with him. The vice chief's son was tormented, demon-possessed, and no one could help. Dano fasted and prayed for three days. Then, near midnight, he went to the shrine where the boy was and did the only thing he knew to do. "I called upon the name of the Lord," he said, "and the demon left the young man." The night the shrines fell silent Villagers said every evil spirit left the village at once. Dano went from shrine to shrine, praying against the darkness that had ruled the place for generations. The vice chief's family, who had braced for his anger, found grace instead. They gave their lives to Jesus, and four more families followed. The people who once opposed him now follow his lead. There is a church in that village today where there used to be shrines. The name of Jesus is still stronger than every dark thing that has ever frightened you. One believer, praying at midnight, was enough to set a whole village free.
content_zh:
牧师达诺在担任牧师之前是一名军人. 他毫无理由地活着走出战场,从未动摇过为什么的感官. "我相信上帝为了某种目的在战场上拯救了我的生命". 宗旨现于一佛村中欲与他无相. 副宰相的儿子被折磨,妖魔吞噬,无人能助.

达诺斋戒祈祷三天. 然后,近午夜,他去了男孩所在的神殿,做了他唯一知道该做的事. "我呼唤天主之名,"他说:"妖魔离开了少年. 夜神社失声村民说 每一个邪恶的灵魂 立刻离开村庄

达诺从神社到神社,祈祷反抗历代统治这个地方的黑暗. 副局长的家族,他为愤怒而坚韧不拔,却找到了恩典。 他们把生命献给了耶稣,还有四个家庭随行. 曾经反对他的人现在遵循他的路线。 今天村里有一座教堂 曾经有神社

耶稣的名字仍然比每件令你害怕的黑暗事物更强大. 一个信徒在午夜祈祷 足以让整个村庄自由

title: They locked the pastor in a psychiatric ward. He led a hundred men to Jesus
title_zh: 他们把牧师关进了精神病病房。他带领一百人归向耶稣
content: Pastor Bakhytzhan Kashkumbaev was an elderly man when Kazakhstan arrested him in May 2013. The charges were strange, that he had harmed a church member's health and stirred up religious hatred. They sentenced him toward ten years and put him in a psychiatric ward, where inmates were routinely drugged. On the way in, he thought it might be the end of his mind. "This is probably the last time I will talk to you in my right mind," he said. Then a question reached him, the kind God uses. "Where is your faith?" Under the cover of the risen Lord Something lifted. "I felt like I was under the cover of the risen Lord," he said. The old man who expected to lose himself instead found Jesus nearer than the walls. He started talking to the men around him. To a prisoner wrecked by drug addiction he said simply, "Only Jesus can help you." Over nine months inside, nearly one hundred inmates gave their lives to Christ. "In prison," he said, "the Holy Spirit opened one dimension of prayer to me." The place meant to break him became the most fruitful pulpit of his life. They released him in early 2014. He walked out having planted the good news in the last place anyone would look for it. God is not locked out by any door that locks you in. He was already inside, waiting.
content_zh:
2013年5月哈萨克斯坦逮捕Bakhytzhan Kashkumbaev牧师时,他是一位老人。 指控是奇怪的,他伤害了一名教会成员的健康并煽动了宗教仇恨。 他们判处他十年监禁,并把他关进精神病病房,囚犯经常在那里服药。 进来的路上,他觉得这也许是他心智的终结.

"这可能是我最后一次在正确的思想中和你说话,"他说. 然后,一个问题来到他身上,神用的那种。 "你的信仰在哪里?" 在升起的上帝的掩护下 有东西解除了 "我觉得自己在升天主的掩护下,"他说. 期待失去自我的老人却发现耶稣比墙壁更靠近. 他开始和周围的人交谈

对一个吸毒成瘾的囚犯来说 他只是说 只有耶稣才能帮助你 里面有九个月,近一百名囚犯为基督献出了生命。 "在狱中",他说"圣灵为我打开了祈祷的一个维度". 打算打破他的地方成为了他一生中最有成果的支点. 他们于2014年初释放了他。

他走了出去 埋下了好消息 在最后的地方 没有人会寻找它。 上帝不会被任何锁住你的门锁住 他已经在里面等了

title: Her church offering came to the exact amount of her power bill, to the penny
summary: 🇺🇸United States· 2020s
title_zh: 她的教会奉献金刚好等于她的电费，一分不差。
content: Lina Johnson did not have enough to cover her power bill. She had told no one the amount. Not a friend, not her church, no one. It was her private worry, the kind you carry quietly and hope somehow resolves. That same week an offering came around at church for a family in need, and Lina gave what she could. Twenty-six cents. It was almost nothing, and she gave it anyway. Down to the penny The next day a friend told her the rest of the story. The offering the church had taken was for her. And when they counted it, it came to the exact amount of her power bill. To the penny. "The offering they took in church yesterday was for me," Lina said, "and it was the exact amount as my power bill. It was to the penny and I never told anyone how much my bill was." Here is the detail that undoes you. Had she given more than her twenty-six cents, the total would have overshot the bill, and the provision would have lost its edge. Even her small gift was part of God's arithmetic. God is not rounding up or guessing. He knew the number she never spoke aloud, and He met it precisely, through people who had no idea. The Father who counts the hairs on your head knows your bill too, down to the last penny.
content_zh:
莉娜·约翰逊没有足够的钱来支付她的权力法案. 她没有告诉任何人这个数额。 不是朋友,也不是她的教堂,没有人 这是她的私人担忧, 你悄悄地携带的, 希望某种程度上解决。 在同一周,教堂里出现了一具供奉物,供奉一个有需要的家庭,莉娜尽了力. 26分钱. 几乎什么都没有,她还是给了它。

下到一分钱 第二天,一个朋友告诉她了其余的故事. 教堂的供奉是给她的 当他们数起来时, 她的权力法案的准确数额就到了。 至一分钱. "他们昨天在教堂里接受的献礼是给我的,"莉娜说,"这是确切的金额,就像我的权力法案.

我从来没有告诉任何人我的账单是多少". 这是让你难受的细节 如果她付出超过26美分,总额会超过法案,而规定会失去优势. 她的小礼物也是上帝算术的一部分 神不是围观或猜测。

他知道她从不大声说话的号码 他通过不知道的人 准确地认识了这个号码 算你头上头发的神父也知道你的帐单 一直到最后一分钱
